items.title: Burkina : 300 élèves sous-officiers de la Gendarmerie prêt à servir la nation
items.description: Burkina : 300 élèves sous-officiers de la Gendarmerie prêt à servir la nation Bobo-Dioulasso, 11 sept. 2026 (AIB) – La 52è promotion des élèves sous-officiers d’actives de la Gendarmerie (ENSOG), a effectué sa sortie de fin de formation ce vendredi, au camp Ouezzin-Coulibaly de Bobo-Dioulasso. La cérémonie a été présidé par le ministre d’État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense Patriotique, le Général de Division Célestin Simporé et placé sous le parrainage du ministre d’État, ministre de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le Commandant Ismaël Sombié. Présidant la cérémonie, le ministre d’État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense Patriotique, le Général de Division Célestin Simporé, a salué la sortie de la 52e promotion des élèves sous-officiers de la gendarmerie, baptisée « Kawgou », qui signifie « victoire » en langue fulfuldé. Selon lui, ces nouveaux sous-officiers viennent renforcer les capacités opérationnelles de la gendarmerie nationale, dans un contexte marqué par les défis liés à la défense du territoire et à la sécurité des populations. A cet effet, il a exhorté les nouveaux gendarmes à s’inscrire pleinement dans la dynamique actuelle du Burkina Faso et à faire preuve de loyauté, de fidélité, de discipline, de courage et de détermination dans l’exercice de leurs missions. Le chef d’État-Major de la gendarmerie nationale, le Colonel Issa Yaguibou, a souligné que cette formation a été axée autour de trois dimensions fondamentales et indissociables, à savoir la formation morale, le développement de la discipline et les valeurs conformes à l'éthique et à la déontologie militaire. Il a félicité les nouveaux Sous-Officiers pour leur brillants résultats obtenus. Tout en les souhaitant une très bonne carrière, il les a invités à défendre avec honneur et dévouement la patrie. Le délégué de la promotion, Jean Donal Zongo s’exprimant aux noms de ses camarades a réaffirmé leur engagement à défendre la mère patrie jusqu’au sacrifice suprême. « Nous n'avons pas de motifs de craindre, et nous devons garder ferme notre engagement, celui de défendre la patrie, la loi et l'honneur au péril de nos vies. Nous n'avons pas à faillir face à notre mission, car nous avons confiance en la formation réussie » a-t-il déclaré. Officiellement entrée en formation le 26 octobre 2024, la 52e promotion compte un effectif total de 300 élèves sous-officiers dont 15 personnels féminins. Après deux années de formation intense, la promotion a achevé sa formation avec une moyenne générale de 15/20. La cérémonie a été marquée entre autres par des allocutions et le port d'épaulettes de Maréchal des Logis aux nouveaux Sous-officiers. Agence d’Information du Burkina GF/GO/OSAR/wis

items.title: D’Athènes à Dakar, le voyage des « Argonautes » sénégalais
items.description: Comme les héros de la mythologie grecque embarqués pour une quête exceptionnelle, les membres de la délégation sénégalaise ont quitté Dakar, mardi, avec une mission singulière : aller chercher la Flamme olympique et la ramener au Sénégal. Mission accomplie depuis jeudi soir. Dans la mythologie grecque, le mythe de Jason et des Argonautes raconte l’une des grandes expéditions héroïques. Comme Jason et ses compagnons, partis jadis à la conquête de la Toison d’or, les Sénégalais ont traversé le ciel pour aller chercher un symbole précieux. Leur mission : recevoir la Flamme des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (Joj) et la ramener à Dakar. Cette fois-ci, donc, point de navire Argo. Le vaisseau est un avion. Mardi passé, à l’aéroport Blaise Diagne de Diass, les valises se ferment, les passeports sont vérifiés et les derniers échanges se multiplient. Chacun mesure que ce voyage n’est pas un déplacement comme les autres. Conduite par Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, président du Comité national olympique et sportif sénégalais (Cnoss) et du Comité d’organisation des Joj (Cojoj), et accompagnée des ministres Clothilde Djirèye Coly, chargée de la Jeunesse et des Sports, et Abdou Lahad Ndiaye, chargé des Transports, la délégation sénégalaise compte également plusieurs personnalités du sport et de la vie publique : Ibrahima Wade, Coordonnateur du Cojoj, Baidy Agne, vice-président du Cnoss, Abass Fall, maire de Dakar, Augustin Senghor, ancien président de la Fédération sénégalaise de football et actuel maire de Gorée, Lamine Niang, directeur général de la Sspp «Le Soleil», et Pape Alé Niang, directeur général de la Rts. Mais cette délégation emporte avec elle bien plus que des bagages. Elle porte la promesse des premiers Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse organisés en Afrique. Concile sénégalais Après sept heures de vol, les « Argonautes » sénégalais apparaissent dans le ciel grec au petit matin du mercredi. Sous leurs pieds, Athènes. L’Acropole domine la ville et le Parthénon rappelle que cette terre fut celle des dieux, des héros et des philosophes, et qu’elle est désormais, un peu, celle du Sénégal. Ici, chaque pierre semble porter une histoire. Mais la délégation n’est pas venue uniquement contempler les vestiges de la Grèce antique. Elle vient accomplir une mission : recevoir un symbole vieux de plusieurs millénaires et lui faire prendre la direction de Dakar. À peine quatre heures plus tard, c’est déjà l’heure du terrain. Place à la répétition générale au stade Panathénaïque. Colonnes, vestiges, tribunes en marbre et lumière méditerranéenne composent un décor qui semble sorti d’un récit mythologique. La cérémonie est répétée dans les moindres détails. Les gestes sont millimétrés, les déplacements réglés, les costumes ajustés. Musique, prises de parole, chorégraphies : rien n’est laissé au hasard. « Dakar est prête » Aux premières heures du jeudi 10 septembre, ils sont là, les « Argonautes sénégalais », en quête de la Flamme. L’attente est longue, mais les officiels sénégalais, grecs et internationaux s’installent aux côtés du public. Loin des contingences politiques, les Sénégalais discutent et trouvent des solutions à tout… ou presque. Loin du pays, les barrières semblent tomber, les chapelles politiques et idéologiques s’effacer. Ce concile olympique est mis entre parenthèses par le début de la cérémonie. De son ouverture, à 11 h 30, heure grecque, jusqu’à sa fin, à 12 h 23, plusieurs moments forts se succèdent. Il y a les frissons provoqués par la voix de Kya Loum, chantant a cappella l’hymne national sénégalais, « Le Lion rouge ». Puis l’allumage de la Flamme, de manière ancestrale et ingénieuse, dans le pays de Zeus. Une flamme qui renaît. Il y a aussi les larmes de la Zimbabwéenne Kirsty Coventry, présidente du Cio, submergée par l’émotion de voir Dakar devenir la première capitale africaine de l’Olympisme. Puis le discours de Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, qui clame : «L’Afrique est prête, Dakar est prête». Enfin, la Flamme est remise au Sénégal. L’histoire s’est écrite sous nos yeux. La délégation sénégalaise est happée par l’événement. Chacun mesure progressivement la portée de ce moment. Les visages s’illuminent. Les congratulations se multiplient. On se prend dans les bras. La mission est accomplie. La Flamme va désormais quitter sa terre d’origine pour entamer un autre voyage. Elle traversera la Méditerranée pour rejoindre Dakar. Il est 23 h 13 sur le tarmac de l’aéroport international Blaise-Diagne. Après plusieurs minutes d’attente et sous l’œil vigilant d’un comité d’accueil soucieux qu’aucune image ne soit diffusée, Birame Senghor et Maurice Diouf, les gendarmes chargés de garder la Flamme, descendent les escaliers de l’avion « Esprit Teranga » avec l’objet tant attendu. Ils s’engouffrent dans un van, étroitement entouré par la cohorte de sécurité, et disparaissent dans la nuit, éclairée par la Flamme et l’espoir de tous les Sénégalais. Comme pour Jason et sa « délégation », c’est mission accomplie pour les « Argonautes » sénégalais. Moussa DIOP, envoyé spécial à Athènes (Grèce)

items.title: Mouhoun/Tournoi de la fraternité de Kona : Le Real s’adjuge le trophée aux tirs au but face au Napoli
items.description: BURKINA -MOUHOUN-KONA-SPORT-JEUNESSE Mouhoun/Tournoi de la fraternité de Kona : Le Real s’adjuge le trophée aux tirs au but face au Napoli Kona, 10 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Le Real de Kona a remporté, le jeudi 09 septembre 2026, la finale du tournoi de la fraternité en venant à bout de Napoli aux tirs aux buts par le score de 4 buts à 3, au terme d’une rencontre âprement disputée et soldée par un score nul et vierge au temps réglementaire. La commune de Kona était en fête le jeudi 09 septembre 2026 à l’occasion de la grande finale du tournoi de la fraternité, organisée dans le cadre des activités socio-culturelles et sportives des élèves et étudiants. Placée sous le haut patronage du Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Kona, Ali Sanou, la compétition a mis en avant les valeurs de fraternité, de cohésion sociale, de fair-play et de dépassement de soi. Pour cette finale très attendue, Napoli affrontait le Real de Kona. Devant un public venu nombreux, les deux formations ont livré une partie engagée, marquée par des duels intenses et plusieurs tentatives de part et d’autre. A la pause, les deux équipes se sont séparées sur un score nul et vierge. Malgré les efforts déployés en seconde période, aucune des deux formations n’est parvenue à trouver le chemin des filets. L’arbitre central, Drissa Yedan, a alors sifflé la fin du temps réglementaire, contraignant les deux équipes à se départager à l’épreuve fatidique des tirs au but. A cet exercice, le Real de Kona s’est montré plus adroit en transformant quatre tirs contre trois pour Napoli, décrochant ainsi le trophée de cette édition du tournoi de la fraternité. Avant le coup d’envoi, le représentant du chef de village, Yacouba Yedan, a souhaité la bienvenue aux autorités, aux joueurs et aux différents participants, tout en formulant des bénédictions pour le bon déroulement de la finale. Le délégué des élèves et étudiants, Mamadou Cissé, a, pour sa part, exprimé sa reconnaissance aux autorités et à l’ensemble des participants pour leur mobilisation. Le PDS, a salué l’initiative et encouragé les deux équipes à faire preuve de fair-play et de respect mutuel. Après son intervention, les autorités présentes ont échangé avec les joueurs, leur prodiguant conseils et encouragements avant de donner le coup d’envoi de la rencontre, sous les acclamations du public. La cérémonie s’est achevée par la remise des trophées et récompenses aux équipes participantes, dans une ambiance festive et fraternelle. Cette finale de cette compétition initiée par les élèves et étudiant de Kona montre que le sport demeure un cadre de rapprochement, de partage et de consolidation de la cohésion sociale. Rendez-vous est pris pour la prochaine édition. Agence d’information du Burkina BB/SB/HB/OO

items.title: Ghana’s economy has moved from standing on broomsticks to concrete pillars – Mahama
items.description: President John Mahama says Ghana’s economy has moved from being vulnerable to external shocks to becoming more resilient, likening the change to a shift from “broomsticks” to “concrete pillars.” Speaking at a citizens’ engagement during his tour of the Upper West Region, President Mahama said the economy in the past would easily collapse whenever there were major developments in the global economy. “In the past, Ghana’s economy used to stand on broomsticks. As soon as something happens in the world, it comes crashing down.” He said the economy is now stronger and capable of withstanding major external shocks. “Today Ghana’s economy is standing on concrete pillars. So even when there’s an earthquake, the country is still standing.” President Mahama said the Iran-Israel-US conflict would have had a more devastating impact on Ghana’s economy in previous years. “In the past, this Iran-Israel-US war, if it had happened some years back, by now the economy would have come crashing down.” He said the economy has been well managed despite the effects of developments in the external environment. “But happily it’s been well managed.” President Mahama added that Ghana could have recorded stronger economic growth this year, potentially reaching 7%, but for the impact of external developments. “We would have made more progress this year than even last year. I’m sure the growth would have hit 7%, but of course we live in this world and we can’t help but be affected.” He maintained that the economy remains solid, although the pace of progress has been slowed by developments in the external environment. President Mahama also said preparations for the 2027 Budget have begun, with budget hearings currently underway. “There’s going to be the new budget 2027, and the budget hearings have currently started, and I’m sure that we’ll capture as many of the essential things that we need to capture as possible.”

items.title: Systemic vulnerabilities within banking industry remain broadly subdued- BoG
items.description: The Bank of Ghana has disclosed that its macroprudential assessment at the end of June 2026 showed that systemic vulnerabilities within Ghana’s banking industry remain broadly subdued. According to its July 2026 Monetary Policy Report (MPR), macro-financial risks have continued to moderate amid improving macroeconomic conditions, declining sovereign risk perceptions, and strengthening investor confidence. It, however, stated that the credit-to-Gross Domestic Product (GDP) gap remains negative but is gradually improving, signalling a recovery in private-sector credit growth while indicating limited risks from excessive leverage. It mentioned that the banking sector continues to exhibit strong capitalisation, liquidity, profitability, and strong asset quality, with contagion risks remaining well-contained. Notwithstanding these favourable developments, downside risks arising from geopolitical tensions and potential external shocks warrant continued vigilance. It promised to continue to support sustained macroeconomic stability, enhance supervisory discipline, and promote prudent risk management practices to safeguard financial stability while supporting sustainable economic growth. The financial soundness indicators in the first-half of 2026 generally strengthened during the review period, with the Sector’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) improving year-on-year, supported by recapitalisation efforts and sustained profitability across the industry. Although the non-performing loans (NPL) ratio declined, the Bank of Ghana said the underlying asset quality risks remain and continue to pose a potential challenge to the sector. Overall, the banking sector’s outlook remains favourable, underpinned by strong capitalisation, sustained profitability, and a resilient financial position that enhances its ability to withstand emerging risks and support economic activity.

items.description: BURKINA-MOUHOUN-BONDOUKUY-CNIB-AES-ENRÔLEMENT Mouhoun/Carte d’identité burkinabè de l’Alliance des Etat du Sahel : 371 personnes enrôlées grâce à une opération de proximité Bondoukuy, 10 sept. 2026 (AIB)-A l’initiative de la Coordination nationale des associations de veille citoyenne (CNAVC), section communale de Bondoukuy, une opération spéciale organisée du 8 au 10 septembre 2026 dans la commune a permis à 371 personnes d’être enrôlées pour l’établissement de la Carte d’identité biométrique de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel (CIB-AES). Pendant trois jours, une équipe de l’antenne de l’Office national d’identification (ONI) de Dédougou, conduite par son premier responsable, Siaka Bako, avec l’appui de la Brigade territoriale de gendarmerie de Bondoukuy, a sillonné les localités de Bouénivouhoun, Koumana et Bondoukuy-centre pour rapprocher les services d’identification des populations. L’opération a été organisée sous la supervision du responsable de la Coordination nationale des associations de veille citoyenne (CNAVC), section communale de Bondoukuy, Seydou Zongo. Elle a permis aux personnes enrôlées de disposer de documents d’identité, en prélude à la marche-meeting prévue le 30 septembre 2026 à Bouénivouhoun, à l’initiative de la CNAVC, section de Bondoukuy. Pour camarade Zongo, cette opération traduit une volonté de répondre concrètement aux besoins des populations en facilitant leur accès aux services d’identification. Il a salué la disponibilité et l’engagement de l’équipe de l’ONI de Dédougou ainsi que l’accompagnement des forces de sécurité dans la réussite de l’activité. Le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Bondoukuy, Lazare Bado, a également salué cette initiative de proximité qui contribue à lever les difficultés d’accès des populations aux documents d’identité. Cette action s’inscrit dans la continuité des initiatives déjà menées dans la commune. Agence d’information du Burkina TT/SB/HB/OO

items.title: Brahim Diaz refuse son jour de repos et retourne à l’entraînement du Real Madrid
items.description: Brahim Diaz ne semble pas vouloir lever le pied. Malgré les efforts consentis lors de la récente rencontre du Real Madrid face à l’Inter Milan, où il a disputé 80 minutes et livré une prestation remarquée, l’international marocain aurait choisi de renoncer à son jour de repos pour se présenter à l’entraînement du club merengue. Selon les informations rapportées par El Chiringuito TV, Brahim Diaz se serait ainsi rendu à la séance d’entraînement du Real Madrid alors qu’il bénéficiait initialement d’une journée de repos. Une décision qui témoigne de son implication et de sa volonté de maintenir un niveau de préparation élevé. Quelques heures auparavant, le Marocain avait été titularisé face à l’Inter et avait participé activement à la prestation madrilène. Présent pendant 80 minutes sur la pelouse, Diaz s’est distingué par son activité et sa capacité à apporter du danger dans le secteur offensif. Alors qu’il aurait pu profiter pleinement de la journée de récupération accordée par le staff, le joueur aurait donc préféré poursuivre son travail au centre d’entraînement. Un choix qui illustre son ambition de s’imposer durablement au sein de l’effectif madrilène. Une implication qui ne passe pas inaperçue Le comportement de Brahim Diaz est particulièrement scruté depuis son retour au premier plan avec le Real Madrid. L’international marocain cherche à gagner en régularité et à occuper une place toujours plus importante dans les plans de l’équipe. Son choix de se présenter volontairement à l’entraînement lors de son jour de repos pourrait être perçu comme un signe supplémentaire de sa détermination. À Madrid, où la concurrence est particulièrement forte, chaque détail compte pour les joueurs qui souhaitent s’imposer dans la durée. Le Marocain semble ainsi vouloir profiter de chaque occasion pour progresser et convaincre son entraîneur. Son investissement quotidien pourrait également lui permettre de maintenir sa condition physique et de rester prêt à répondre présent lorsque le Real Madrid fera appel à lui. « En mission » Cette attitude a rapidement suscité des réactions sur les réseaux sociaux et auprès des observateurs du club. Brahim Diaz est présenté comme étant « en mission », une formule qui résume la détermination affichée par le joueur. Après une nouvelle performance encourageante face à l’Inter, le Marocain semble donc déjà tourné vers les prochaines échéances. Son objectif est clair : continuer à travailler, gagner la confiance du staff et s’imposer davantage dans un effectif madrilène particulièrement compétitif. Cette volonté pourrait être un atout important pour la suite de sa saison. Avec un calendrier chargé et une forte concurrence à son poste, la capacité de Diaz à rester disponible et performant pourrait jouer un rôle déterminant. Pour l’heure, son retour volontaire à l’entraînement, malgré un jour de repos, constitue surtout un nouveau témoignage de son état d’esprit. Brahim Diaz semble déterminé à saisir chaque opportunité pour s’imposer au Real Madrid et à poursuivre sur la dynamique affichée face à l’Inter. The post Brahim Diaz refuse son jour de repos et retourne à l’entraînement du Real Madrid appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ECP promotes four officers to BS-20, transfers 54 across country amid reshuffle
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has announced a major administrative reshuffle, promoting four BS-19 officers to BS-20 and transferring 54 BS-17 officials across the country with immediate effect. The orders, issued with the approval of the Chief Election Commissioner, also include key postings at the provincial and secretariat levels. According to a notification, four officers have been promoted from BS-19 to BS-20 on a regular basis and placed on one-year probation. The promoted officers include Fazal Hakeem and Abdul Lag. Hakeem, the Regional Election Commissioner in Peshawar, has been posted as Additional Director General (Elections-II) at the ECP Secretariat in Islamabad. Lag, Director (Elections) at ECP Balochistan, will serve as Joint Provincial Election Commissioner (Elections) in Balochistan. Khurshid Alam, Director to the CEC, has been posted as ADG to the CEC. The ECP has also upgraded and redesignated his previous BS-19 post. Nazar Abbas, ADG (Electoral Rolls) OPS, has been posted as ADG (Electoral Rolls) at the ECP Secretariat and promoted to BS-20. In a related notification, Syed Waseem Ahmed Jafri, Joint PEC (Elections), BS-20, has been transferred from Balochistan to Sindh. 54 BS-17 officers transferred The largest set of changes came through another notification, which ordered the transfers and postings of 54 Assistant Election Commissioners and Assistant Directors in BS-17. The transfers cover all four provinces and involve wide-scale movement between field offices and the ECP Secretariat in Islamabad. Several officers have been brought to the Secretariat to serve in key wings, including Confidential, Protocol, HRMS, Record and LGE. Among those transferred to the Secretariat are Zoya Kanwal as Assistant Director (Confidential), Ayesha Hamid as AD (LGE-KP), Adil Ahmad Shahzad as AD (Protocol), and Syeda Javeria as AD (HRMS). Field postings include Shabir Ahmed Shah, who has been moved from REC Rakhshan to DEC Kharan; Imran Khan Abbasi, from REC Shaheed Benazirabad to DEC Shikarpur; and Shahab Siddique, from DEC Bannu to PEC Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

items.title: Kourwéogo/AG-CPSA : Les acteurs de la sécurité alimentaire alertent sur les effets de l’exploitation minière
items.description: BURKINA-KOURWEOGO-SECURITE-ALIMENTAIRE Kourwéogo/AG-CPSA : Les acteurs de la sécurité alimentaire alertent sur les effets de l’exploitation minière Boussé, 12 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Les acteurs de la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle du Kourwéogo ont examiné le vendredi 11 sept, les enjeux de l’exploitation minière sur la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, à l’occasion de la première session ordinaire de 2026 de l’Assemblée générale du Conseil provincial de sécurité alimentaire (AG-CPSA). La rencontre de la première session ordinaire de 2026 de l’Assemblée générale du Conseil provincial de sécurité alimentaire, tenue sous le thème « Exploitations minières et sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle dans la région de Oubri : enjeux et perspectives », a permis de faire le point sur la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages, la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027 et les interventions des différents acteurs. Le secrétaire général de la province, Harouna Kombasséré représentant le président du Conseil provincial de sécurité alimentaire, a appelé les acteurs à renforcer la coordination de leurs interventions et à privilégier les synergies afin de dégager des solutions adaptées aux réalités de la province. Selon la présentation faite aux participants, l’exploitation minière peut contribuer à la sécurité alimentaire à travers la création d’emplois, le développement des marchés locaux, le financement d’activités génératrices de revenus et la réalisation d’infrastructures hydrauliques, sanitaires et routières. Elle comporte toutefois des risques, notamment la réduction des superficies agricoles, la pression sur le foncier, la diminution des espaces pastoraux, la modification des pistes à bétail et la pression sur les ressources en eau. La réduction de la main-d’œuvre agricole et la hausse du coût de la vie figurent également parmi les impacts relevés. Dans le Kourwéogo, l’activité minière est notamment pratiquée par la mine industrielle Nordgold Niou SA et par des orpailleurs sur les sites de Guesna, Kalwin, Zipélin et Silmiougou. Les acteurs recommandent notamment la mise en œuvre effective du plan de gestion environnementale et sociale afin d’atténuer les impacts négatifs de l’activité minière. La campagne agropastorale 2026-2027 connaît une installation tardive et irrégulière des pluies. Les mois de juin et juillet ont été marqués par une insuffisance et une mauvaise répartition des précipitations, entraînant des retards dans les opérations culturales. Une amélioration a été enregistrée en août, permettant la poursuite des travaux agricoles. Toutefois, les cultures présentent une physionomie jugée passable et certaines localités ont connu un stress hydrique sévère au début du mois de septembre. Pour soutenir les producteurs, l’Etat et ses partenaires ont notamment distribué 119,848 tonnes de semences améliorées à prix subventionné et 762,35 tonnes d’engrais. Quelques 112,7 hectares de bas-fonds et 366,4 hectares dans le cadre de la conservation des eaux et des sols, de défense et de la restauration des sols dégradés ont également été aménagés. Dans le domaine pastoral, plus de 400 000 animaux ont bénéficié de vaccinations grâce aux produits vétérinaires subventionnés dans le cadre de l’Offensive agropastorale, hydraulique et halieutique (OAPHH). Pour la campagne 2025-2026, la production céréalière disponible dans la province est estimée à 44 569 tonnes, contre des besoins évalués à 37 575 tonnes. La production maraîchère s’est établie à 15 165,7 tonnes. Malgré cette disponibilité, les stocks paysans sont jugés faibles. Les prix des principales denrées alimentaires ont connu une baisse en juillet 2026 par rapport à la même période de 2025, mais la viande, le poisson et les légumes restent relativement chers. Sur le plan nutritionnel, le taux de malnutrition aiguë globale est estimé à 11,3 % dans la province. La prise en charge affiche toutefois un taux de guérison de 93,9 % entre janvier et juillet 2026. A la fin des travaux, les participants ont recommandé une meilleure coordination des actions sur le terrain. Agence d’information du Burkina DB/HB/OO

items.title: Burkina: poursuite de la lutte contre les pratiques spéculatives dans les Koulsé
items.description: (Kaya, le 12 septembre 2026) Dans le cadre du contrôle intensif des produits de grande consommation, la Direction régionale de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat des Koulsé (DRICA-Koulsé) mene, depuis le 7 septembre 2026, une opération d’inspection intensive dans la commune de Kaya. Durant cette période, près d’une trentaine de points de commerce ont fait l’objet de contrôles par les équipes de la DRICA-Koulsé. Les principales infractions relevées au cours des vérifications portent sur le défaut de publicité des prix, la pratique de prix illicites et la non-déclaration des lieux de stockage de produits destinés à la vente. Ces manquements ont conduit à la saisie d’une vingtaine de bouteilles de gaz pour pratique de prix illicites. Un avertissement ferme a également été adressé à un contrevenant pour non-déclaration de son lieu de stockage. Celui-ci a été convoqué à la DRICA-Koulsé pour accomplir les formalités de déclaration. La Direction régionale réaffirme son engagement à poursuivre la lutte pour la protection des consommateurs. Elle rappelle aux commerçants l’obligation de déclarer auprès de la DRICA-Koulsé les lieux de stockage des produits destinés à la vente et les exhorte à adopter des comportements exemplaires. DCRP/MICA DRICA-Koulsé L’article Burkina: poursuite de la lutte contre les pratiques spéculatives dans les Koulsé est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire’s export sectors face heightened risks due to El l Niño – Fitch Solutions
items.description: Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire’s export sectors face heightened risks, as the October-December cocoa crop development period coincides closely with the expected peak in El Niño conditions, Fitch Solutions has revealed. According to the UK-based firm, lower rainfall and higher temperatures during key pod-development stages could reduce yields, thereby weighing on export earnings, government revenues and rural incomes. It added that very strong conditions could disrupt crop cycles, lift food inflation, strain hydropower output and raise social unrest risks. From a food security and inflation perspective, it pointed out that rice imports account for a substantial share of consumption across several markets, including Senegal (69%), Côte d’Ivoire (49%) and Ghana (47%), leaving these markets exposed to an El Niño-driven tightening in global rice supplies. It disclosed in its recent report that Sub-Saharan Africa faces numerous risks. In East Africa, Fitch Solutions pointed out that El Niño is typically associated with stronger October-December short rains, potentially resulting in flooding, crop damage, disease outbreaks and transport disruptions, reflected in its Environmental Sustainability and Governance (ESG) Country Risk data on shares of the population exposed to flooding. At the same time, many East African economies remain highly exposed to global wheat prices given high import dependency, implying that any sustained increase in global grain prices arising from ongoing Black Sea disruptions could exacerbate inflationary pressures further, even if domestic harvests benefit from stronger rainfall. Commodity Exporting Nations Face Additional Risk It continued that commodity-exporting economies would face an additional risk through weaker prices, which would erode export earnings, fiscal revenues and foreign exchange inflows. “Copper and gold exporters are especially vulnerable to more hawkish US monetary policy. Regarding crude, while we forecast prices to come in lower as the US-Iran conflict reaches a preliminary agreement, there is a risk that prices are weaker than we forecast, particularly if markets continue to react bearishly to positive developments and the Fed hikes rates anyway”, it added.

items.title: CM Bugti says 'no dialogue' with those taking up arms against state
items.description: Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti said on Saturday there would be “no dialogue in any case” with those who took up arms against the state. He made the remarks while speaking via video link to the country’s media anchors, senior journalists and other representatives at the Chief Minister’s Secretariat on Saturday, according to a statement issued by his office. CM Bugti said the war against terrorism would continue in Balochistan until the “last terrorist” was eliminated, adding that it was not possible to control the entire province while sitting in Quetta. He affirmed that the civil and military leadership were united against terrorism and there was “no ambiguity or confusion” on the matter. The chief minister noted that security forces were performing their duties in difficult circumstances in Balochistan, adding that state institutions were working in complete coordination in the fight against terrorism. Before the talk with journalists, CM Bugti was also provided multiple briefings covering the provincial government’s strategy for social and economic development, governance and service delivery, effective use of development funds, and measures to ensure that development projects benefited the people. A briefing on minerals and mining highlighted the sector’s potential, ongoing projects and measures being taken to develop it and better utilise the province’s mineral resources, the statement said. The Ministry of Interior and Tribal Affairs also briefed the chief minister on the law and order situation, the Provincial Action Plan, police reforms and progress on the integration of the Levies Force into the police, the statement added. Bugti was also briefed on the Safe City project, legislation and coordination among law-enforcement agencies. During the interaction with journalists, CM Bugti also expressed his views on the creation of new administrative units, saying, “If new provinces are to be created in Balochistan, they should be on administrative rather than linguistic grounds.” On Thursday, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the Parliament was expected to debate the issue of new provinces next month. Speaking to mediapersons, Bugti said he had no knowledge of any “ two-and-a-half-year government agreement ” for Balochistan, according to the statement. The decision to change the government had to be taken by the political leadership, he said, adding that his cabinet would continue to serve the people as long as they were in office. The chief minister was quoted as saying that although he could not claim that corruption across the province had been completely eliminated, it had decreased compared to the past. Measures were being taken to ensure merit in all government departments, including educational institutions, he added. He said development projects in Balochistan had been completed in record time compared to the past, adding that the provincial government was focused on making the development process effective, result-oriented and aligned with public needs. Referring to the return of foreign nationals, Bugti said that 1.1 million Afghan refugees, along with other foreigners, had been sent back to their homeland from Balochistan. On the issue of missing persons, he said the matter was sometimes presented on national media and other forums without proper context, which did not reflect the true picture of the situation. “Terrorism was not an issue of one province but of the entire country and required joint efforts at the national level for its elimination”, Bugti was quoted as saying.

items.title: Nahouri : Le Lions Club Ouagadougou Phénix plante des arbres pour préserver l’environnement
items.description: BURKINA-NAHOURI-ENVIRONNEMENT Nahouri : Le Lions Club Ouagadougou Phénix plante des arbres pour préserver l’environnement Pô, 7 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Le Lions Club Ouagadougou phénix district 403 A3 a organisé le samedi 5 septembre 2026 dans la commune de Tiébélé, une série d'activités caritatives dans le cadre d'un reboisement organisé chaque année dans leur bosquet situé dans le village de Lo-Longo en présence des autorités administratives, coutumières et du président mandat 2026-2027, Geoffroy Bationo. Le Lions Club Ouagadougou Phénix 50, district 403 A3, a renoué avec sa tradition annuelle en se rendant, le samedi 5 septembre 2026, dans la commune de Tiébélé pour y mener une série d’activités. Reboisement, dépistage de la vue, don de lunettes, de fournitures scolaires, du matériel d'assainissement à la mairie de Tiébélé et un repas statutaire et communautaire ont meublé la journée. Le premier acte de cette sortie dans la commune a été le dépistage de la vue et don de lunettes de correction à plus d’une centaine de personnes vulnérables dépistées. Aussi sur place, le deuxième vice-président de la délégation spéciale de Tiébélé Loussé Pouakia a réceptionné du matériel d'assainissement au profit de la commune. Les membres du club ont ensuite mis le cap dans le village de Lo-longo, situé à une dizaine de kilomètres à l’Est de Tiébélé-Centre où les attendait une mobilisation des grands jours. Ils ont été accueillis au rythme de la musique locale avec en tête leur chef coutumier. Ils ont visité leur bosquet mis en place il y a de cela 14 ans C’est avec beaucoup d’enthousiasme que le Chef du village de Lô-Longo a encore reçu la délégation des Lions. Pour lui, l’amitié date de très longtemps et les expressions musicales du jour en témoignent. «Je peux vous affirmer que ce bosquet profite aux populations. Chaque année les fournitures scolaires qu’ils viennent donner aux élèves soulagent beaucoup les parents. Parce qu’il y a des parents qui n’arrivent pas à donner à temps des cahiers aux enfants pour qu’ils commencent les cours », s’est exprimé l’autorité coutumière. Le président du mandat 2026-2027 du club, Geoffroy Bationo, a déclaré qu’ils étaient plus que satisfaits. «Nous venons mettre les plants en terre et la protection est assurée par le village. Nous sentons qu’il y a vraiment de l’engouement derrière cette activité. Ce qui témoigne de l’intérêt que tout le village avec en tête son chef ont pour les activités que nous organisons», a soutenu le camarade Bationo. Cette activité a été parrainée par African Mining Partenaire SARL et co-parrainée par Damien Zoungrana. Cette journée a été clôturée par un repas statutaire et communautaire dans une ambiance conviviale. Agence d’information du Burkina AY/HKO/HB/OO

items.title: Norway’s Princess Astrid dies two days after attending brother King Harald’s funeral
items.description: Princess Astrid of Norway, the sister of the late King Harald V, has died at the age of 94, two days after attending his funeral, the country’s royal palace has announced. The new king, Haakon VIII, said that “throughout her long life, Princess Astrid represented the Royal House in a warm and dutiful manner”. Harald died last month, aged 89, after more than 35 years as king. His funeral was Astrid’s last public engagement. The princess will be buried at state expense and flags will be flown at half-mast across Norway, Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said. Astrid was the last surviving child of King Olav V, who reigned from 1957 to 1991. She became Norway’s first lady at the age of 22 in 1954, after the death of her mother Crown Princess Märtha. Olav did not remarry and Astrid retained the title until her brother’s marriage in 1968. “In her work, Princess Astrid was always particularly concerned with care and inclusion for the most vulnerable in society,” her nephew King Haakon said in his statement. Her health had deteriorated in recent months and in March she received hospital treatment for pneumonia. Dozens of European royals and heads of state attended Harald’s funeral on Wednesday, including the Prince of Wales and three Nordic kings. Thousands of people lined the route during a procession from the royal palace to Oslo Cathedral on Wednesday afternoon. The non-royal leaders paying their respects included Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and five foreign prime ministers. In the final months of Harald’s life, Norway’s royal family faced personal challenges and scandal. Earlier this year, documents revealed that King Haakon’s wife, Queen Mette-Marit, had had frequent contact with US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. She later said she wished she had never met the late disgraced financier. Meanwhile, her son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Høiby – who is not a royal but grew up within the family – was given a four-year jail term for two counts of rape in June. Høiby, who is under house arrest pending appeal, was granted permission to attend the funeral.

items.title: La guerre en Iran creuse l’écart de croissance entre les BRICS et le G7
items.description: Les pays du Golfe , européens et plusieurs grandes économies asiatiques figurent parmi les plus impactées par la guerre en Iran, notamment en raison de la perturbation des approvisionnements énergétiques et de la hausse des prix du pétrole et du gaz. Les entreprises énergétiques américaines ont quant à elles vu leurs bénéfices exploser . Malgré cela, les perspectives de croissance des États-Unis pour 2026 ont reculé entre janvier et juillet, selon les projections du Fonds monétaire international (FMI), passant de 2,4 % à 2,3 %. D’ailleurs, tous les autres pays membres du G7 – Canada, France, Allemagne, Italie, Japon et Royaume-Uni – ont vu leurs perspectives de croissance être révisées à la baisse après le lancement de la guerre contre l'Iran. Parmi les 7 pays membres du groupe, seulement deux (les États-Unis et le Canada) devraient ainsi connaître une croissance supérieure à 1 % cette année. Parmi les cinq pays fondateurs des BRICS – Chine, Russie, Inde, Afrique du Sud et Brésil –, un seul (l’Afrique du Sud, avec -0,3 point) a vu sa croissance revue à la baisse. Des facteurs exogènes à la guerre au Moyen-Orient expliquent ces écarts : l'économie brésilienne bénéficie d'une hausse de ses exportations agricoles vers la Chine, tandis que la croissance indienne continue d'être portée par la consommation domestique et les services. La guerre a moins d’impact sur les perspectives de croissance des BRICS que sur celles des pays du G7 dans leur ensemble. En moyenne (non pondérées par le PIB), les pays du G7 devraient connaître une croissance de 0,97 % en 2026, selon les dernières perspectives de juillet du FMI. C’est plus de deux points de moins que les cinq pays fondateurs des BRICS, pour qui la croissance moyenne devrait atteindre 3,12 %. L’écart de croissance moyenne entre les deux blocs, qui se situait à 1,68 point en janvier, soit avant la guerre, a ainsi augmenté de 0,5 point et atteint désormais 2,15 points. L’article La guerre en Iran creuse l'écart de croissance entre les BRICS et le G7 est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.description: La compétion d'athlétisme entamée ce samedi 12 septembre 2026 a consacré une bonne moisson pour les athlètes burkinabè. Les Étalons ont remporté l'épreuve des 100 mètres masculins grâce à Ibrahim Sawadogo (10,94s) devant le Nigérien Moucharaf Oumarou (10,97s). Abdoul Rachid Traoré du Burkina termine 3e (11,16s). Aux 800m filles, Yasmine Yé qui a battu le record national cadet avec ses 2'14″60. est arrivée première devant sa compatriote Roukiatou Sylla (2'16″84.) et Farida Zakari Nana du Niger (2'34 »). Djakalia Traoré a porté haut les couleurs nationales burkinabè à l'issue de la course de 1500 mètres en franchissant en premier la ligne d'arrivée suivi du Nigérien Amadou Moumouni. Rasmané Ouédraogo complète le tableau. Les Burkinabè ont aussi dominé le lancer de poids. Les filles se sont adjugé les deux premières places avec Zalissa Zongo qui a réalisé un jet à 11,56 m et Chérifa Djibo (9,82m). Djamila Saloy du Niger repart avec la médaille de bronze dans cette épreuve avec une marque à 9,07m. En l'absence des représentants maliens, la compétition qui a concerné les U18 a été disputée entre Burkinabè et Nigériens. Les premiers au classement dans chaque épreuve sont récompensés d'une enveloppe de 400 000 FCFA. La compétition se poursuit demain 13 septembre à partir de 16 au stade du 4 août. items.title: China's Xi urges Brics to oppose sovereignty violations, protectionism
items.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Brics member states on Saturday to oppose sovereignty violations and reject protectionism, speaking at a summit in India, Beijing’s state media reported. The conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, along with global trade turbulence and energy security, dominated the two-day meeting of the 11-nation bloc. Xi told the gathering that Brics should “oppose violations of other countries’ sovereignty and interference in their internal affairs, [and] constructively participate in resolving hotspot issues,” according to state news agency Xinhua . Other leaders attending the summit in New Delhi include Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, whose country has been at war since US-Israeli strikes against it on February 28. “As the situation in the Middle East and the Gulf region continues to evolve, the war there has caused serious losses to people across the region,” Xi said, calling on countries to “uphold the authority of the United Nations” in his remarks, Xinhua reported. On trade, the Chinese president urged countries to “reject all forms of protectionism” and “support the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organisation at its core”. The comments come less than two weeks before Xi’s expected visit to Washington, a major trade rival of Beijing. Later, in a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the summit, Xi said China views ties with India from a “strategic, long-term perspective,” Xinhua added . “China and India can learn from each other’s strengths and achieve shared development,” the state news agency quoted Xi as saying. Earlier today, he arrived in New Delhi for the summit alongside leaders from India, Russia and Iran as wars, trade and energy test the divided grouping. His visit is also being closely watched as his first to neighbouring India since 2019, and the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the nuclear-armed rivals. Xi was given a red-carpet welcome, with an honour guard of soldiers and traditional dancers in colourful dresses. His arrival comes six years after a deadly 2020 military clash along their disputed Tibetan border, with ties gradually improving through restored flights, visas and high-level contacts. Beijing said on Friday it was “ready to work with India … by strengthening communication, enhancing cooperation, and properly handling differences”. The underlying territorial dispute remains unresolved, and both sides retain heavy military deployments along their roughly 3,500-kilometre high-altitude border along Tibet. ‘Substantial harvest’ Xi is due to hold face-to-face talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi later on Saturday, according to New Delhi’s foreign ministry. “They are looking for ‘early and substantial harvest’ when it comes to the border issue,” said Pradeep Taneja, a China-India expert at the University of Melbourne. “You cannot have a build-up of your forces on the border … but at the same time say ‘we should continue to have people-to-people relations and economic relationships’.” Deep mistrust remains, with their contested Himalayan frontier, a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry still complicating ties. Dozens of Tibetans protested in New Delhi on Friday — exiles, like their Buddhist leader the Dalai Lama, who has lived in India since fleeing a Chinese crackdown in 1959 — waving placards against Xi’s visit. Modi embraced Putin on Friday before talks. The Russian president, who last visited India in December 2025, is one of New Delhi’s most important strategic partners. India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the US-Iran war in part by turning to Russia, despite Moscow’s war in Ukraine and pressure from Washington and other Western capitals. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, also in New Delhi on Friday, said that pressure on Iran “has reached a critical and dangerous stage” following the “military aggression by the United States and Israel”. Modi and Pezeshkian also held talks. India maintains cordial relations with Iran and Israel, but is also careful to strike a delicate balance in its ties with Washington. ‘Big constraint’ Brics was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers. Modi told leaders that Brics nations “represent 50 per cent of the world’s population, 40pc of global GDP, and more than 2pc of global trade”. As well as Iran, Brics includes Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates — countries with sharply differing positions on the war launched by the US and Israel in February. UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi are also to attend. Brazil is represented by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva campaigning for a fourth term in October elections. Brics foreign ministers failed to agree on a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May. “The Gulf conflict is going to be the central fault line this time during the Brics summit,” said Harsh V Pant of India’s Observer Research Foundation. “What was seen until last year as an achievement — the expansion of Brics — today looks like a big constraint on Brics,” Pant said.

items.title: NCA awards 700MHz spectrum to MTN Ghana for US$109.9m
items.description: The National Communications Authority (NCA) has advanced the process of assigning spectrum in the 700 MHz, 2.3 GHz and 3 GHz bands for mobile broadband services, including 5G. In a statement issued on Thursday, September 11, the NCA said it had opened and ranked the Best Price Offers submitted by qualified applicants at the NCA Tower. Scancom Plc (MTN Ghana) emerged as the sole qualified and successful applicant for the 700 MHz band, securing two lots — the maximum number that can be awarded to a single applicant under the Request for Applications (RFA). The two lots attracted a combined licence fee of US$109.9 million, bringing the allocation process for the 700 MHz band to a close. For the 2.3 GHz band, five lots were available, with four applications submitted by Ghana Telecommunications Company Limited (Telecel Ghana) and GoIP Telecommunications Ltd. The band is therefore under-subscribed, and the next stage of the allocation process will proceed in accordance with the RFA. Meanwhile, demand has exceeded available spectrum in the 3 GHz band. The NCA said three lots were available, while four applications were submitted by Scancom Plc (MTN Ghana) and Ghana Telecommunications Company Limited (Telecel Ghana). The Authority said the next stage of the process for the 3 GHz band would also proceed in accordance with the RFA. The NCA will announce the final outcome for the 2.3 GHz and 3 GHz bands after the remaining stages of the licensing process have been completed. Successful applicants for those bands will also be notified separately. Read the full statement below

items.title: Saudi Arabia shuts key oil pipeline after drone attack launched from Iraq
items.description: Saudi Arabia has closed a critical oil pipeline after it was attacked by drones launched from Iraq, as conflict in the Middle East widens. Iraq said it had fired a military commander and launched an investigation after admitting the drone attack on its neighbour’s East-West pipeline had originated in one of its provinces bordering Iran. The 1,200km (745 mile) pipeline has helped Saudi Arabia – the world’s largest crude oil exporter – bypass the Strait of Hormuz. The incident comes amid a major advance by the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, putting more pressure on global oil shipping routes as the US-Iran war stretches into its seventh month. On Friday, Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces said they had struck Houthi fighters in the strategic coastal city of Mokha, a day after the Houthis seized control of the entire Red Sea coast. Riyadh on Friday said it had shut the pipeline as a precaution, as satellite images of scorched ground and smoke near the site emerged. The foreign ministry said the attack resulted in some injuries and damage, which was still being assessed. The pipeline has been moving 4% to 5% of global oil supply, news agency Reuters has reported, citing ship tracking companies and analysts. Saudi Arabia has chosen not to retaliate at this stage, its foreign ministry says, following a call from Iraq’s prime minister. It said the kingdom would “support the efforts of the Iraqi government” to “prevent attacks” launched from the country against neighbouring states. “The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia affirms that it reserves its right to take all necessary measures to safeguard its sovereignty and security, protect its facilities, and ensure the safety of its citizens and residents,” the statement added. The Iraqi prime minister’s office in its own statementsaid the operations commander in the Maysan governorate – a province which borders Iran – had been removed from his post following confirmation the drone attack had been launched from that region. The Gulf Co-operation Council – made up of representatives from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and Kuwait – also issued a missive condemning the attack. “This attack represents a dangerous escalation and an unacceptable threat to the security of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, its territorial integrity, and its vital installations, as well as a flagrant violation of the principles of international law,” secretary general Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi. This week, a lightning advance in Yemen has also seen Houthi militants seize control of much of the country’s coastline, sources say. The group said it had control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the gateway to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal, though it said maritime navigation is “safe for all companies except for Saudi vessels”. The Yemeni Armed Forces have since struck back. On Friday, spokesman Majid al-Nuzaili said they had targeted Houthi positions in and around the city of Mokha, adding that they had destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed a number of Houthi fighters. The strategic coastal city on the Red Sea is situated about 80km (50 miles) north of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The Houthis seized control of Mokha on Thursday. Their attack drove many people to flee to Aden, where Yemen’s internationally recognised Presidential Leadership Council and government are based. Local sources also reported that government forces carried out air strikes targeting Houthi forces in Taiz governorate, which is along the Red Sea coast, and Ibb governorate, which neighbours Taiz. The developments have squeezed both sides of the Arabian Peninsula, pushing crude oil prices to over $100 a barrel for the first time since July. Fears over inflation have risen with the spike in energy prices, further pushing up government borrowing costs.

Passenger train derails in France leaving at least 44 injured
items.description: At least 44 people have been injured, including one seriously, after a passenger train derailed in northern France, local officials have said. An 18-year-old woman was airlifted in critical condition by helicopter to hospital. The officials said 186 passengers were on board the train that was operating between Rouen and Caen in Normandy. Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said 140 firefighters and other emergency teams were deployed to the scene of the crash on Friday evening near Cléon, just south of Rouen. The cause of the crash was not immediately known, but reports in the French media suggest it could have been an act of sabotage. The authorities have not commented on the issue. Local authorities activated a mass-casualty response plan after the crash shortly before 20:00 (18:00 GMT). “Suddenly there were a few jolts, and then after about three seconds it got stronger and stronger,” Louis, a passenger on the train, told ICI Normandie radio. “I couldn’t stay in my seat any more. The windows partially shattered, the stones from the track came into the carriage. It was really shocking. I’m still shaking,” he added. Photographs later emerged showing passengers leaving the train, three of whose carriages had overturned, according to French media.

items.title: Ukraine faces ‘toughest winter’ since Russia’s full-scale invasion, UN official tells BBC
items.description: Ukraine is facing its “toughest winter” since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, a top United Nations official told the BBC. Alexander De Croo, head of the UN development agency, said there was a risk of “humanitarian catastrophe” if Russian attacks cut off access to power and water. Speaking in Ukraine, De Croo – the UN’s third most senior official – accused Russia of systematically targeting the country’s energy infrastructure. He said there was now a “race against the clock” to repair the power network before winter sets in and temperatures plummet. Russia and Ukraine have been intensifying aerial attacks in recent months, and both deny deliberately targeting civilian infrastructure. Russia has started to use faster, jet-powered drones that are harder to intercept in recent around-the-clock attacks on Ukraine – and in particular Kyiv. Many of the strikes have targeted Ukraine’s infrastructure, including businesses, warehouses, factories, petrol stations, as well as energy infrastructure. Ukraine continues to launch drone strikes deep into Russian territory, largely against gas, oil and business distribution facilities. Both countries deny targeting civilians. Deadly attacks have resumed after US President Donald Trump sent envoys for talks in Moscow with Russian President Vladimir Putin and in Kyiv with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky last weekend. Five people were killed and 67 others were wounded in a daytime Russian drone strike on a shopping mall in Pavlohrad, a city in Dnipropetrovsk region, on Thursday, Ukrainian officials say. Earlier in the week two other shopping malls were targeted by Russian air strikes, killing two people and injuring 28 people in the attacks on the cities of Zaporizhzhia and Sumy. Russia reported a Ukrainian seaborne drone attack on the resort city of Sochi overnight on Wednesday, in which 28 people were wounded, as well as three more deaths blamed on Ukrainian attacks. Two people were also killed earlier this week when Russian drones hit a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova, which has increasingly found itself caught up in the conflict. A full-scale war has been raging between Russia and Ukraine since Putin launched an invasion more than four and a half years ago. De Croo, a former prime minister of Belgium, told the BBC: “This winter is going to be the toughest one since the war”. He said Ukraine started “from a very weak base going into this winter”. He added the UN were “very, very worried… about what this winter could become.” The concerns are driven by what De Croo said was Russia’s “very systematic” targeting of civilian and energy infrastructure. “This is petrol stations, it’s shopping malls, it’s business centres, but it’s especially energy infrastructure, energy transmission lines, and so on. There is absolutely no justification for that,” he said. This could lead a “worst-case scenario” where people struggled to access energy to run heating, and water and sewage systems stopped working. “With the temperatures that you would get here that would lead to circumstances which would be really close to humanitarian catastrophe,” De Croo said. Winter temperatures in Ukraine can drop to -20C. If power supplies and critical infrastructure were severely damaged it could lead to “quite some human suffering”, De Croo said. Under efforts to prepare Ukraine for winter the UN Development Programme is helping to rebuild parts of its energy system that were damaged last winter. It is also establishing more sustainable and decentralised energy plants, which are less vulnerable to attack. De Croo said completing the difficult and dangerous work was “almost an impossible task”. “They are reconstructing these sites under constant, constant air alarms. And they know that they are working at a site which is a target,” he said. “So you try to reconstruct, but part of your day you can’t work because it’s just too dangerous.”

items.title: Close race in Sweden as hard right eyes role in government
items.description: Sweden’s left- and right wing political blocs are in a tight race in Sunday’s general election, with current conservative Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson promising cabinet jobs for hard-right allies if he remains at the helm. Latest polls show a narrow lead for the left grouping, which is backing the Social Democrats’ Magdalena Andersson to return to power. Kristersson has been supported in government by the hard-right Sweden Democrats (SD), who have neo-Nazi roots. National security, gang crime and welfare spending are among the key issues, but the potential for the anti-immigration SD to enter government could also influence the outcome. In Sweden, there are two major political blocs – with four parties on the right and four on the left, so Swedes are used to coalition and minority governments. More than eight million people are eligible to vote in the election for Sweden’s Riksdag. A poll on Friday, commissioned by Swedish news service Ekot, shows the left-wing bloc with 50.8% of the vote, compared with the right-wing bloc on 47.6% – a lead of 3.2%. The centre-left Social Democrats, who have pledged higher public spending, lead the polls, with 28.6%, while on the right the Sweden Democrats are behind them with 18.3%, according to the Ekot survey. Other opinion polls on Friday also put the left-wing bloc in the lead. The Social Democrats have regularly led Swedish governments since World War Two and have been the country’s dominant political force for much of the last century. In stark comparison the SD, founded by Nazi sympathisers in the 1980s, were for decades shunned by the mainstream. But the last election in 2022 marked a watershed moment, with the SD becoming Sweden’s second largest party following a campaign focused on issues around immigration and violent crime. They have since offered outside support to the current centre-right coalition, which has overseen a dramatic tightening of migration policy, including the abolition of permanent residency for refugees and increased deportations. But the party’s MPs have never held ministerial roles. The Sweden Democrats have experienced controversies during this election campaign, including allegations that a party official spread pro-Russian messages on social media. Kristersson has said the official should be fired if the claims turn out to be true, while SD leader Jimmie Åkesson said the party was investigating the allegations. Nicholas Aylott, associate professor of political science at Södertörn University, told the BBC that the party getting into government “would be another big step in the normalisation of the party”, but added that it was not the main issue for voters. “That said, it might still be important for the election outcome,” he said. Aylott explained that some voters who would have backed centre-right parties may well switch allegiance to the opposition, because they are put off by the prospect of SD ministers. Although he thought they would be few in number, “they might just tip the balance against the incumbent right-wing bloc”, he said. This weekend’s election comes a week after Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) came close to winning a majority in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. They topped the poll with almost 44% of the vote, and their local leader Ulrich Siegmund says he is in talks with another party and other MPs in the hope of taking control of parliament.

items.title: Fermeture d’un oléoduc saoudien : le pétrole à 150 $ dès lundi ?
items.description: Le monde entier retient son souffle. Alors que les prix de l’énergie et des carburants sont plus hauts depuis des années, le pétrole pourrait flamber et atteindre la barre des 150 dollars dès l’ouverture des marchés lundi 17 septembre. C’est l’inquiétude exprimée par l’expert en énergie Damien Ersnt. Citée par RTL Info, M. Ersnt redoute une envolée spectaculaire des prix de l’or noir après la décision prise vendredi 11 septembre par l’Arabie saoudite de fermer l’oléoduc Est-Ouest qui a été ciblé par des drones en provenance d’Irak. L’Arabie saoudite ferme un important oléoduc « Je pense qu'on va s’orienter sans doute vers un baril à 150 dollars s’ils n’arrivent pas à réparer rapidement le pipeline », alerte Damien Ernst, professeur à l’ULiège et expert en énergie. Pour lui, la fermeture de l’oléoduc saoudien risque de s’étaler dans le temps. Au moins une station de pompage a été « complètement détruite », selon cet expert et elle « risque de prendre des semaines, voire, des mois pour la réparer ». Cet oléoduc transporte 7 millions de barils de pétrole par jour. Il est utilisé par Riyad pour contourner la fermeture du détroit d’Ormuz. Ce pipeline joue un rôle important dans la poursuite des exportations pétrolières de l’Arabie saoudite depuis l’éclatement de la guerre américano-israélienne contre l’Iran fin février dernier. Flambée des prix du gazole aux États-Unis et en France Vendredi, le ministère saoudien des Affaires étrangères a condamné « le ciblage du pipeline Est-Ouest dans les régions de Ryad et de Médine par plusieurs drones en provenance d'Irak » et fait état « de blessures humaines et de dommages qui sont en cours de réparation ». Ces attaques ont fait flamber les cours du pétrole vendredi qui ont frôlé la barre des 110 dollars vendredi, pour la première fois depuis mai dernier. Cette hausse des prix du pétrole n’a pas tardé à impacter les prix des carburants en France où le litre de gazole a atteint 2,7 euros. Aux États-Unis, le gallon (3,785 litres) de gazole a grimpé à 6 dollars pour la première fois de l’histoire. Les Français subissent la flambée des prix des carburants avec un gazole qui flirte avec les 2,40 € le litre dans certaines stations-service de la Sarthe et proche des 2,70 € sur l’autoroute. L’article Fermeture d'un oléoduc saoudien : le pétrole à 150 $ dès lundi ? est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Adutwum’s spokesperson challenges Haruna’s claim he inherited current CSSPS
items.description: Spokesperson for former Education Minister Yaw Osei Adutwum has challenged Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu’s claim that he inherited the Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS), arguing that the current application being used for the process was introduced under the Mahama administration in 2025. Yaw Opoku Mensah was reacting to a publication attributed to Mr Iddrisu in which the Education Minister was quoted as saying, “The CSSPS system is not perfect, but I inherited it, and we’ve improved it.” He said the claim did not reflect the history of the system, insisting that the application currently being used to run the placement process, COLDSIS, was a third-party application introduced in 2025. According to him, COLDSIS is different from the system that had been developed and used over the previous seven years. “Hon. Minister, you cannot inherit what you introduced,” Mr Opoku Mensah said. He argued that since COLDSIS was introduced under the current administration as an intervention to improve the placement process, the government must also accept responsibility for both its successes and shortcomings. “You cannot introduce a new application, oversee its implementation, encounter serious challenges in its operation, and then turn around and tell Ghanaians that those particular challenges were inherited from the previous administration,” he stated. Mr Mensah said the government must be transparent about the origins and performance of the placement application instead of attributing its current challenges to the previous administration. He maintained that Ghanaians deserved accountability on the management of the placement process. “Ghanaians deserve transparency and accountability, not an attempt to rewrite the history of a system simply to escape responsibility for its present challenges,” he said. He urged the Education Minister and the government to accept responsibility for the outcomes of COLDSIS. “Take the credit when it works. Take responsibility when it fails,” Mr Opoku Mensah added.

items.title: Flawed NEV incentive
items.description: THE draft New Energy Vehicle policy gets its destination right. Electrifying transport, cutting the oil import bill and building an export-oriented auto industry are worthwhile goals. But the incentive structure chosen to achieve them rewards the wrong technology. The main flaw is treating plug-in hybrid and battery electric vehicles as interchangeable. Both qualify for the same 1pc sales tax on CKD units and NEV inputs — as if a PHEV running mostly on petrol delivers the same environmental pay-off as a BEV. It does not. Pretending otherwise weakens the policy’s stated purpose. Weak charging infrastructure and real range anxiety discourage Pakistani consumers from buying BEVs. Subsidising PHEVs just as heavily hands them an easier option, which will show up as progress on paper while doing little to build the charging network or battery-vehicle demand the transition actually needs. PHEV assemblers received generous concessions under the last auto policy but never delivered localisation or built charging infrastructure. Repeating that arrangement will invite the same outcome: subsidised assembly with no real technology transfer. Taxing conventional hybrids at 25pc, up from 8.5pc, while cutting PHEV tax to 1pc, amounts to picking a winner through the tax code rather than market competition. That stalls transition towards genuine transport electrification while penalising Japanese manufacturers who built much of Pakistan’s auto parts ecosystem. A more coherent policy would reserve the sharpest incentives for BEVs, and let others compete on their actual emissions and fuel-savings performance. Consumers, not tax brackets, should decide which of these technologies wins as charging infrastructure improves and prices come down. The rest of the draft holds up. Export targets, tighter localisation rules and incentives tied to auto-parts exports could finally push manufacturers to build for international markets, instead of just assembling for domestic buyers. But those incentives need to reward genuine export growth and local value addition, not simply subsidise the same low-localisation assembly model that has defined the industry for decades. Published in Dawn, September 12th, 2026

items.title: ECG’s problems are about management, not ordinary workers – TUC
items.description: Deputy Secretary-General of the Trades Union Congress (TUC), Dr Kwabena Nyarko Otoo, has described the challenges facing the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) as a management problem rather than a failure of the company’s ordinary workers. He has questioned why Ghana should consider handing ECG to a foreign private entity when the country has qualified people capable of managing the power distributor. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, September 12, during a discussion on private sector participation in ECG, Dr Otoo said the responsibility for the company’s difficulties rests largely with those appointed to oversee its operations. “The ECG problem is a management problem. Who appoint the managers?” he asked. He said some arguments being made about ECG’s inability to operate effectively were troubling enough to raise questions about Ghana’s capacity to manage its own institutions. “In fact, sometimes, some of the comments make it difficult. It makes us question whether we should have gotten independence in the first place,” he said. “Are we telling ourselves that this country we cannot find competent people to manage ECG?” he asked. The TUC official said ordinary employees of ECG should not be blamed for the company’s financial and operational challenges. “If ECG is a management problem, the challenges with ECG are not the ordinary workers of ECG. Ben Boakye knows that,” he said. He instead pointed to the company’s board and management and raised concerns about how revenues and contracts are handled. “The challenges with ECG are the people, the board members, the managers,” Dr Otoo said. Dr Otoo also raised concerns about contracts within the energy sector, citing an alleged $69 million crude oil transaction. “The challenges with ECG are people who get a contract to supply crude oil and bring in crude oil to the tune of $69 million,” he said. He claimed that the crude oil supplied under the contract was later found to be contaminated and could not be used. “Only for us to find that it’s a contaminated crude that cannot be used,” he said. According to Dr Otoo, political authorities were aware of such problems but failed to take action. “And the political authorities are aware, they are involved, they don’t do anything about it,” he alleged. He questioned why such challenges should then be used to justify selling ECG to a foreign entity. “Then they tell us that the only way out, we cannot help, we cannot stop. So the only way out is to sell the company to a foreign entity,” he said.

items.title: Don’t wait for the floods to recede before going green – Prof Naana Jane
items.description: Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has urged Ghanaians to treat environmental protection and greening as an integral part of national development. She said the recent floods should not be the only trigger for conversations about waste management, drainage and the environment. Speaking on Saturday at the opening of the 14th Ghana Garden and Flower Show, she said the lessons from the floods must continue long after the waters have receded. “That conversation must not end when the floodwaters recede. Keeping Ghana clean and making Ghana greener are part of the same responsibility,” she said. She stressed that Ghana’s approach to development must give greater attention to trees, gardens and green spaces as towns and cities expand. “Greening should therefore not be something we consider after development; greening should be part of development itself,” Prof Naana Jane said. She also linked the country’s environmental agenda to economic opportunities, particularly in horticulture. According to her, gardens and flowers represent more than beauty, with an entire economy involving growers, skills, services, markets and livelihoods. “The opportunity is to help more of these enterprises develop into sustainable businesses that can employ others, supply larger markets, and, where possible, compete beyond Ghana,” she said. Prof Naana Jane said government programmes such as Feed Ghana provide opportunities for the horticulture sector to expand, with vegetables among the priority crops. She pointed to support for irrigation, improved inputs, greenhouse production and market access as areas that could help the sector do more. She also highlighted the establishment of farmer service centres across the country, saying they are intended to bring services closer to producers, including export support, inputs, machinery, and market linkages. The Vice President said the environmental agenda also aligns with the Tree for Life initiative, under which millions of seedlings are being planted. She added that assemblies are being encouraged to work with parks and gardens to improve and maintain green spaces in towns and cities. Prof Naana Jane further challenged stakeholders to create stronger opportunities for young people in horticulture by connecting agriculture with technology, creativity and enterprise. “The opportunity is not only to encourage young people to grow more, but also to help them to see the businesses they can build around their produce,” she said. She called for stronger collaboration among local authorities, developers, businesses, training institutions and financial institutions to grow the green economy. “Green means business,” she said, urging stakeholders to consider how Ghana can become greener while creating businesses and livelihoods.
