items.title: PAM : à Azrou, Lekjaa et Sekkouri détaillent les priorités pour la prochaine étape
items.description: À Azrou, la direction nationale du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) a placé son programme électoral sous le signe de l’action concrète, avec un accent particulier sur l’éducation, la santé, le pouvoir d’achat, l’emploi et l’accompagnement des jeunes. Devant les habitants, Fouzi Lekjaa et Younes Sekkouri ont défendu une vision fondée sur des mesures chiffrées et une volonté affichée d’accélérer le rythme du développement. Lors d’un meeting organisé ce vendredi 11 septembre, Fouzi Lekjaa, membre de la direction nationale du PAM, a insisté sur la nécessité de réduire les écarts de développement entre les territoires. Le responsable politique a rejeté l’idée d’un « Maroc à deux vitesses », estimant que les différentes régions du Royaume doivent pouvoir bénéficier de la richesse nationale et des services publics à un rythme comparable. L’éducation figure parmi les principaux axes mis en avant par le responsable du PAM. Le parti ambitionne de hisser le secteur à des niveaux internationaux, avec l’objectif affiché d’atteindre la sixième place mondiale. Pour Lekjaa, cette ambition n’a rien d’irréaliste, à condition de réunir volonté, qualité des choix et engagement dans la durée. Il a notamment fait le parallèle avec les performances réalisées par le Maroc dans le domaine sportif et footballistique. Le même impératif d’amélioration est appliqué au secteur de la santé. Le programme défendu par le PAM prévoit de renforcer l’accès à des soins de qualité dans les différentes régions et provinces, à travers des infrastructures hospitalières capables de répondre aux besoins des populations et de garantir des conditions de prise en charge jugées dignes. Sur le terrain social, le pouvoir d’achat et le coût de la vie occupent également une place centrale. Lekjaa a souligné les pressions exercées par la hausse des dépenses courantes sur les ménages et présenté l’amélioration des conditions de vie comme l’une des priorités du programme. Parmi les mesures avancées figure notamment une revalorisation des pensions de retraite jusqu’à 3.000 dirhams, ainsi que des dispositions ciblant les veuves et les catégories les plus vulnérables. La jeunesse constitue un autre volet majeur de cette feuille de route. Le PAM entend accompagner les jeunes depuis la formation jusqu’à leur insertion professionnelle et, pour ceux qui souhaitent entreprendre, jusqu’à la création et au développement de leurs activités. L’objectif affiché est de mieux transformer les compétences et les capacités des jeunes en projets créateurs de valeur et d’emplois. Cette approche a été développée par Younes Sekkouri, membre du bureau politique du PAM et ministre de l’Inclusion économique, de la Petite entreprise, de l’Emploi et des Compétences. Il a notamment insisté sur la lutte contre le décrochage scolaire, le soutien aux parcours de formation et la consolidation de la classe moyenne. Pour Sekkouri, l’accompagnement des jeunes ne peut toutefois pas se limiter à la formation. Il doit aussi intégrer une dimension sociale permettant aux bénéficiaires de poursuivre leur parcours malgré les dépenses liées au transport, à l’alimentation et aux autres charges quotidiennes. L’enjeu est d’éviter que les contraintes matérielles ne deviennent un obstacle à la formation et, à terme, à l’accès au marché du travail. Le soutien aux entreprises et l’amélioration de leur capacité à créer de l’emploi complètent ce volet économique. Le PAM lie ainsi l’investissement dans les compétences, l’accompagnement de l’entrepreneuriat et le renforcement de la classe moyenne à son ambition de modifier la trajectoire du développement. Le discours prononcé à Azrou a également été marqué par une critique de certaines situations observées au niveau local. Lekjaa a notamment pointé les insuffisances persistantes dans plusieurs communes de la province de Boulemane, citant l’accès à l’eau, l’assainissement et les routes. Il a opposé ces besoins de première nécessité aux promesses électorales qui, selon lui, réapparaissent à l’approche des échéances. Le responsable du PAM a, dans ce contexte, invoqué le principe de responsabilité et de reddition des comptes, en visant la gestion de plusieurs communes de la province. Mais au-delà de cette charge politique, il a surtout assuré que son parti entend traiter les difficultés territoriales à travers des mesures concrètes plutôt que par des engagements sans lendemain. Cette volonté résume, selon Lekjaa, le positionnement du PAM pour la prochaine phase : accélérer le rythme du développement, réduire les disparités territoriales et agir sur les principaux facteurs qui pèsent sur le quotidien des citoyens. Le responsable politique a ainsi repris l’image du train à grande vitesse Al Boraq pour illustrer l’ambition d’un Maroc qui doit, selon lui, avancer au rythme de l’action et des résultats plutôt qu’à celui des promesses renouvelées à chaque échéance électorale. Le parti présente cette orientation sous le slogan du « changement de cap », avec l’investissement dans le capital humain, le renforcement de la classe moyenne, l’amélioration des services publics et l’accompagnement économique des jeunes comme principaux leviers. Lekjaa reconnaît la difficulté de mettre en œuvre de telles réformes, tout en estimant que leur réussite demeure possible à condition de réunir compétence, choix appropriés et engagement dans l’action. items.title: Gabon : le président Oligui Nguema somme Airtel et Canal+ de construire leurs sièges
items.description: Le president gabonais Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema a hausse le ton, le 10 septembre, a l'egard d'Airtel Gabon et de Canal+ Gabon, leur demandant de passer rapidement des projets presentes sur maquette a la construction effective de leurs sieges sociaux. Lors d'une visite de chantiers, le chef de l'etat a directement interpelle les representants des deux entreprises, reclamant des preuves concretes du lancement des travaux. Il a averti que les terrains accordes par l'etat pourraient leur etre retires en l'absence de realisation des projets, allant jusqu'a evoquer la possibilite de voir les operateurs quitter le pays. Airtel dans le viseur Concernant Airtel, present au Gabon depuis 26 ans selon les echanges rapportes, Oligui Nguema a deplore que l'operateur ne dispose toujours pas de son propre siege et continue de louer des locaux. Le president gabonais a egalement evoque des dettes d'environ 20 milliards de francs CFA que la societe devrait a des tiers, tout en s'interrogeant sur les investissements structurants realises par l'operateur au regard des benefices tires de sa presence sur le marche gabonais. Le chef de l'etat a ainsi demande a Airtel de concretiser son projet de siege, plutot que de se limiter a la presentation de maquettes. Canal+ egalement interpelle Canal+ Gabon a recu une mise en garde similaire. Oligui Nguema a exige que l'entreprise passe, elle aussi, a la phase de construction effective de son siege. Le president a notamment evoque la situation de Canal+ au Burkina Faso, ou les activites du groupe avaient ete suspendues avant une renegociation, afin d'illustrer la possibilite de mesures similaires si les engagements pris au Gabon n'etaient pas respectes. Cette intervention s'inscrit dans la volonte affichee par les autorites gabonaises de renforcer le suivi des investissements et de conditionner les avantages accordes aux entreprises a la concretisation de leurs projets.

items.title: Big Chef Season 5: Final 10 face Omo Tuo Challenge
items.description: The final 10 contestants on Big Chef Season Five will face the Omo Tuo Challenge this Sunday as the competition intensifies. Following the season’s first eviction, the contestants return to the Big Chef kitchen knowing that the margin for error is becoming smaller as the race for the ultimate prize continues. Last week’s Jollof Challenge proved to be one of the most eventful episodes of the season so far. After two previous appearances in the bottom two, Michael staged an impressive comeback, delivering a plate of Jollof that put him in contention for the Star Chef of the Day title. His performance resulted in a tie with Clara, but after weighing both dishes, the judges decided Clara had done enough to take the top spot, earning her the Star Chef title. At the other end of the competition, Jeremiah, Grace and Yayra found themselves in the bottom three. Jeremiah was eventually saved, while Grace and Yayra became the first contestants to be evicted from Big Chef Season Five , reducing the number of young chefs from 12 to 10. Now, the remaining contestants must put last week’s emotions behind them as they face the Omo Tuo Challenge. Omo Tuo, popularly known as rice balls, is a well-loved Ghanaian dish typically served with soup and a variety of accompaniments. While the dish may be familiar to the young chefs, getting the texture of the rice balls right, preparing the perfect accompaniment and delivering the flavours the judges are looking for could prove challenging. With only 10 contestants remaining, every challenge becomes increasingly important, and another strong performance could move one young chef a step closer to the ultimate prize. Who will master the Omo Tuo Challenge? Who will emerge as the next Star Chef of the Day, and who could find themselves at the bottom? Find out when Big Chef Season Five airs this Sunday at 4:00 pm on Joy Prime. Viewers can also catch the contestants on JP Diaries every Tuesday at 5:00 pm on Joy Prime. items.title: Suspected vehicle theft kingpin arrested in Ogun
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a 28-year-old suspected vehicle theft kingpin, Mosuru Issa, and recovered a stolen wine-coloured Toyota Camry along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. Issa, of Osungboye Street, Agege, Lagos State, was arrested by operatives of the Mowe Divisional Police Headquarters during a routine stop-and-search operation along the Mowe axis of the expressway. The police said the suspect was arrested at about 7:30 a.m. on Friday, after the occupants of the vehicle allegedly abandoned it and fled upon sighting the operatives. In a statement issued on Saturday, the Ogun State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, said the conduct of the occupants aroused the suspicion of the officers, who immediately gave chase. “Three occupants, on sighting the police, suddenly abandoned the vehicle and fled in different directions, raising suspicion,” the statement said. According to the command, the officers pursued the fleeing occupants, leading to the arrest of Issa, while the vehicle was secured and recovered. Preliminary investigation, the police said, revealed that the vehicle had allegedly been stolen on September 7, 2026, from where it was parked in Ojoo, Lagos State. The command said efforts were ongoing to locate the owner of the vehicle and arrest the two other occupants who escaped from the scene. The case has subsequently been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, SCID, Eleweran, Abeokuta, for further investigation. Commenting on the development, the Commissioner of Police, Ogun State Command, CP Bode Ojajuni, commended the operatives for their vigilance and swift response. Ojajuni, according to the statement, reaffirmed the command’s commitment to proactive policing and sustained operations aimed at protecting lives and property while disrupting vehicle theft, highway crime and other criminal activities across the state. The command stressed that the recovery demonstrated the importance of routine patrols, proactive policing and lawful stop-and-search operations in detecting criminal activities and recovering stolen property. The police also warned criminals against using Ogun highways as escape routes, assuring residents that the command would continue to intensify security operations across the state. Vehicle owners were equally advised to adopt basic security measures, including the use of tyre locks, steering locks and other appropriate anti-theft devices, especially when parking in public or unsecured locations. items.title: Trump says Houthis have asked US not to intervene in Yemen
items.description: United States President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthi fighters, who have seized a vital shipping corridor linking Europe and Asia, have asked Washington not to intervene. The Houthis have taken control of Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast after capturing three strategic islands in a lightning offensive. Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest oil exporter, has relied on the area ever since Iran’s Hormuz blockade choked off its shipments via the Gulf. “The Houthis called us and they don’t want to fight with us,” Trump told reporters on a visit to Dublin, Ireland. “They don’t want us to go after them.” He added that “everything’s gonna work out fine and dandy,” in the region. Trump also mentioned having spoken to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, whom he described as a “friend”. According to US outlet Axios , the Saudi crown prince called Trump twice on Thursday to request US strikes on the Houthis, but the American president declined. The Houthis also targeted Saudi Arabian oil facilities this week with a massive drone and missile attack. Yemeni govt forces hit Houthis in Mocha In Yemen, the government forces said on Saturday they have struck Houthi fighters in the strategic Red Sea city of Mocha. Men gesture in a screen grab from a video released on Sept 11, 2026 and said to show Khaled bin Walid camp after Houthis captured the city of Mocha in Taiz Province. — Al-Masirah TV/Handout via Reuters Following a week-long offensive, the Houthis on Friday captured Yemen’s Red Sea coast, cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab strait , a vital artery for Saudi Arabian oil exports as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed amid the US-Iran war. “The armed forces destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed members of the Houthi terrorist militia backed by the Iranian regime,” near the port of the city of Mocha, the government news agency Saba reported. The spokesman for the Yemeni government forces, Majed Abdullah al-Nazili, said they have also struck the Houthis’ “vehicles and members” on the Mocha-Dhubab road, 11 kilometres from the city, according to Saba . Nazili said on Friday they had begun shelling areas in Mocha, and called on citizens not to use the Taiz-Mocha and Mocha-Dhubab roads. The Houthis seized control of Mocha on Thursday, with their attack driving many to flee to Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based. On Friday, Houthi media said two Saudi strikes hit Mocha’s airport , while a local official said the city’s seaport was hit by six missiles of unknown origin. The Houthi offensive, which started last week , has killed more than 500 people, according to sources on both sides. It has also displaced about 46,000 people, the UN migration agency said on Friday. It is part of renewed hostilities in Yemen’s civil war that began with the group’s takeover of the capital Sanaa in 2014.

items.title: IGP not opposed to citizens recording police officers – Media aide
items.description: The Nigeria Police Force has clarified that Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Olatunji Disu is not opposed to citizens recording police officers while carrying out their duties in public. The Force New Media Officer, Aliyu Giwa, said Disu’s concern was with the misuse of such recordings, particularly when police encounters are turned into social media content. Giwa made the clarification in a series of posts on X on Saturday, following criticism of the IGP’s recent comments on Nigerians filming police officers. According to him, the police were not seeking to prevent legitimate scrutiny or deny citizens their rights. “The IGP’s concern is not to shield Police officers from accountability or deny citizens their rights. Instead, it focuses on the misuse of recordings, especially when officers are provoked, ridiculed, filmed for entertainment, or subjected to unnecessary intrusion while performing their duties,” Giwa said. He urged Nigerians to distinguish between documenting police activities responsibly and deliberately exploiting encounters with officers for social media content. “It is important to distinguish between responsible documentation and the deliberate exploitation of Police encounters for social media content,” he said. Giwa noted that legitimate recordings could serve as evidence against misconduct while also protecting police officers from false allegations. “As a public institution, the Police must remain open to legitimate scrutiny. Evidence is essential when an officer acts improperly. Similarly, responsible recording can protect officers from false allegations and support investigations,” he said. He, however, stressed that being a police officer did not strip an individual of basic rights to dignity and privacy. “However, wearing the uniform does not remove an officer’s right to dignity or privacy,” Giwa said. The clarification followed criticism from an X user who argued that the police should equip their officers with body cameras if they objected to citizens recording them. Responding to the criticism, Giwa maintained that Disu had not rejected the practice of recording police officers altogether. “While you are allowed to interpret it as you see fit, the message from the IGP was concerning the misuse of recordings, not a general rejection of legitimate documentation or accountability,” Giwa said. He also disclosed that body cameras were being considered as part of efforts to promote accountable policing. “Body cameras are, in fact, part of the broader conversation about modern, accountable policing, and they can protect both citizens and officers,” he said. Giwa called for a more constructive debate on the issue, saying accountability and citizens’ rights could coexist with professional policing. “The police need to be accountable and citizens should exercise their rights in a responsible way, we can have that discussion without using insults. The end aim is the same, a more professional Police Force and a safer Nigeria,” he said. He also rejected attempts to portray the controversy as a confrontation between the police and the public or between Disu and the Nigerian Bar Association. “Therefore, the conversation should not be framed as Police versus the public or the IGP versus the NBA,” he said. “Instead, it should focus on balancing accountability with responsibility, transparency with privacy, and citizens’ rights with the professional discharge of Police duties,” he added. The clarification followed a recent courtesy visit by the NBA leadership to Disu at the Force Headquarters in Abuja, during which the issue of recording police officers was discussed. Disu had expressed concern about Nigerians recording police officers, particularly for social media skits, describing the practice as “very, very demoralising” for members of the Force. The IGP, however, acknowledged that citizens had the right to record officers performing their duties in public. “We are not saying they cannot exercise their rights of recording officers in the public places while doing their jobs,” Disu said. “But they should put restraints and not turn our police officers to content for their skits or anything,” he added. His remarks triggered criticism from lawyers, human rights groups and other Nigerians, with some arguing that citizens had a constitutional right to document police officers while they were performing their duties in public. NBA President Oyinkansola Badejo-Okusanya had also argued that a distinction should be made between legitimate recording of police activities and intrusion into officers’ private lives. The controversy came after a March 17 judgment of the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, which affirmed Nigerians’ right to record police officers while they perform their duties in public. Giwa said the meeting between the IGP and NBA leadership showed that institutions could hold different views while still engaging constructively. “The engagement between the IGP and NBA leadership demonstrates that strong institutions can engage constructively, clarify positions, and collaborate despite differing perspectives,” he said. He said the way forward was not for the police or members of the public to fear the use of cameras but to ensure that technology was deployed responsibly. “In the digital age, the solution is not to fear the camera. Instead, we should use technology responsibly, uphold professionalism, and let truth, rather than social media narratives, define the conversation,” Giwa said. “The camera should not weaken the institution. Also, institutions should not fear legitimate scrutiny. Both must ultimately serve the truth, justice, and the Nigerian people,” he added. The post IGP not opposed to citizens recording police officers – Media aide appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: England survive scare to seal 3-0 sweep against Pakistan
items.description: England overcame a major wobble to beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the third Test at Edgbaston on Saturday, sealing a 3-0 series sweep. The home team, chasing just 130 to win, were in deep trouble when openers Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay were dismissed in the first over, bowled by Mohammad Abbas. Joe Root, England’s record run-scorer, edged his first ball, bowled by Razaullah, through the slips for four in a nervy start but settled and scored quickly to take the sting out of the situation. The skipper was given a huge reprieve when he chopped onto the stumps off Mohammad Ali, only for the umpire to signal a no ball, leaving the bowler distraught. Root, with Jordan Cox at the other end, had another let-off when he edged an Abbas delivery between first and second slip, with neither fielder moving. But he reached his half-century off 57 balls with a cut for four and Cox matched him shortly afterwards. England reached their target in the 25th over, with Root unbeaten on 62 and Cox 59 not out. Root’s men had appeared set for a quickfire win inside three days on Friday before debutant fast bowler Razaullah launched an audacious assault with the bat, clubbing nine sixes as he raced to 81 off 63 balls. The 21-year-old number nine, who also took four wickets in England’s first innings, put on 121 for the ninth wicket with fellow paceman Abbas (42) as England floundered. “Fair play to Pakistan, they threw some punches last night,” Root told the BBC. “They made it very difficult for us and in some ways it’s a good thing to go through that. “Test cricket is not always going to go your own way. You’re going to have good surfaces to try and find different ways of taking wickets but to see us actually be quite clinical with the bat off the back of that was good too. So in many ways we’re better for it.” Razaullah’s heroics have changed the mood music but they came too little, too late for Pakistan, who have endured a miserable series, losing the first Test by an innings and 103 runs and the second by 194 runs. The tourists sent seven players home after their crushing defeat in the second Test at Lord’s and brought in seven replacements, with Razaullah among them. They also sacked head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul as their tour plunged into chaos. Pakistan made four changes to their side for the third Test and they put up a fight despite being dismissed for a paltry 133 in their first innings. At least, though, the “Raz-ball” fightback in Birmingham showed there was still a pulse ahead of their next assignment against Sri Lanka in October. “We had a couple of good moments. I think we have bowled well but I think the first innings cost us. Too many soft dismissals,” said Pakistan captain Babar Azam. “I think this was a good opportunity for youngsters to play against quality bowlers, quality opponent, so they learned a lot and I think this is helpful for the future.” The 3-0 whitewash is a huge tonic for England, who were in turmoil just weeks ago following a series loss to New Zealand and the exits of head coach Brendon McCullum and captain Ben Stokes. But tougher challenges lie ahead, starting with a Test series in South Africa in December and January, while a home Ashes looms next year.

items.title: Dalla Ngabou : la mairie renforce les infrastructures sanitaires
items.description: La commune de Dalla Ngabou a réceptionné, vendredi 11 septembre 2026, le poste de santé construit à Ngabou. Réalisée par la mairie et équipée par la Fondation 221, à hauteur de 130 millions de francs CFA, l’infrastructure sanitaire devrait bientôt commencer à fonctionner. Les autorités administratives ont promis l’affectation d’un personnel pour assurer la prise en charge des populations. Au nom du maire de la commune de Dalla Ngabou, le premier adjoint au maire, Cheikh Ngom, a exprimé sa gratitude à l’ensemble des partenaires ayant participé à la réalisation de cette infrastructure sanitaire. À l’en croire, la mairie a dégagé, sur fonds propres, une enveloppe de 30 millions de francs CFA, avec l’appui de ses partenaires. Parmi eux, la Fondation 221, qui a assuré l’équipement du poste de santé. En attendant l’affectation du personnel nécessaire au démarrage des soins, Cheikh Ngom a annoncé que la construction de logements destinés à l’infirmier chef de poste et à la sage-femme est également prévue. A lire aussi : Diagane Barka (Foundiougne) : Sorom étrenne son nouveau poste de santé Composés de matériels médicaux, de consommables et d’intrants, les équipements ont été mis à la disposition de la mairie par la Fondation 221. Sa directrice des opérations au Sénégal, en Gambie, en Côte d’Ivoire et en Mauritanie, Sophie Diop, a expliqué que cet accompagnement s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme « La santé pour tous ». À ce titre, la Fondation a mis à la disposition de la commune un conteneur de 40 pieds contenant des équipements médicaux, des consommables et des intrants. Des matériels estimés à 130 millions de francs CFA. Venu présider la cérémonie d’inauguration, le sous-préfet de Ndame, Djidiack Kital, a magnifié les efforts consentis par le maire. Selon lui, ces efforts ont permis de construire le poste de santé dans un endroit stratégique, à proximité de l’autoroute Ila-Touba. Dans la même veine, il a souligné qu’il travaille avec le district sanitaire afin de faire remonter le besoin en personnel exprimé par le maire. En attendant, il estime que le Comité de développement sanitaire (CDS), qui sera installé en collaboration avec la mairie, pourra contribuer à la mise à disposition d’un personnel communautaire. Pour terminer, le sous-préfet a salué le partenariat entre la mairie et la Fondation 221, qui a permis l’équipement du poste de santé. Birane Diop, correspondant

items.title: Meet 68-yr-old Nigerian grandfather who bagged first-class degree in UK
items.description: A 68-year-old Nigerian-born grandfather has graduated with a first-class degree in social work from Goldsmiths, University of London, after returning to education as a mature student. Chris Osagbaekhoe, who was born and raised in Nigeria and now lives in Thamesmead, south-east London, received his BA (Hons) in Social Work at a graduation ceremony at the Queen Elizabeth II Centre in Westminster on September 2. The father of four and grandfather of 12 began his social work studies at the age of 64, driven by a desire to support vulnerable people and advocate for those whose voices are often unheard. Chris had previously studied psychology and counselling between 2013 and 2015 before deciding to pursue a career in social work. “Part of the inspiration was to empower people to empower themselves, and part of the motivation was to be a voice to the voiceless – that was my inner drive,” he said. According to Goldsmiths, Chris experienced setbacks during his academic journey and transferred to the university in 2024 but remained determined to complete his studies. His personal experience with disability also influenced his desire to advocate for others. “There are abilities in disability. My lived experience has given me empathy, understanding and the determination to empower others,” Chris said. He said he hoped his achievement would encourage other mature students and people living with disabilities to pursue their ambitions regardless of their age. “If I can achieve this at 68, others can too. People are often far stronger and more capable than they realise,” he said. Chris also credited resilience, faith and the support he received from Goldsmiths for helping him overcome the challenges he encountered during his studies. “I’m happy there were challenges along the way, but because of resilience and faith, and the support from Goldsmiths University, we are celebrating success today,” he said. The lecturer in social work at Goldsmiths, Dr Carmen Yau, described Chris’s journey as one of “extraordinary determination, courage, and hope”. She said his story demonstrated that education could be transformative at any stage of life and reflected the values of social work, including resilience and belief in people’s potential. Chris is now looking for his first job as a qualified social worker. Beyond his career, he hopes to establish a community-based project or community centre to support young people and help steer them away from crime. A multi-instrumentalist who plays the drums, keyboard, guitar, bass guitar and trumpet, Chris also plans to use his musical talents to inspire the next generation. As he celebrated his graduation, he left other aspiring students with a simple message: “Your dreams do not expire because of your age.” Vanguard News The post Meet 68-yr-old Nigerian grandfather who bagged first-class degree in UK appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Attentats du 11 septembre 2001 : la CIA publie 69 rapports alertant sur la menace terroriste de ben Laden
items.description: L'Agence centrale de renseignement des etats-Unis (CIA) a declassifie 69 rapports de renseignement contenant des avertissements sur les projets du groupe terroriste Al-Qaïda visant a attaquer les etats-Unis avant les attentats du 11 septembre 2001. Ces documents ont ete publies le 11 septembre, exactement 25 ans apres la plus grande attaque terroriste de l'histoire des etats-Unis. Les donnees publiees couvrent la periode allant de fevrier 1998 a septembre 2001. Elles montrent que la CIA informait regulierement les presidents americains Bill Clinton et George W. Bush de la menace representee par Oussama ben Laden et Al-Qaïda. Cependant, les services de renseignement n'ont pas pu determiner l'ampleur ni la nature precise de l'attaque en preparation. Les documents contiennent egalement des avertissements concernant les intentions d'Al-Qaïda d'attaquer les etats-Unis en 1998 et la preparation d'eventuelles operations en 2001. Ainsi, dans l'un des rapports date du 10 septembre 1998, un analyste de la CIA ecrivait qu'Al-Qaïda « pourrait envoyer un avion rempli d'explosifs dans une ville americaine ». En juillet 2001, l'un des rapports faisait etat d'un nouveau report de l'operation terroriste attendue de ben Laden, tout en soulignant que la preparation d'autres attaques pouvait se poursuivre. Pres de 3 000 morts et plus de 6 000 blesses La CIA a egalement publie un rapport de situation adresse au president des etats-Unis a 4h du matin, le 12 septembre 2001. Or, la pratique habituelle de l'agence prevoit la publication de ce type de rapports de renseignement presidentiels environ 40 ans plus tard. Le matin du 11 septembre 2001, 19 membres d'Al-Qaïda ont detourne quatre avions de ligne. Deux d'entre eux se sont ecrases contre les tours du World Trade Center a New York, qui se sont ensuite effondrees. Le troisieme avion s'est ecrase contre le Pentagone, pres de Washington. Le quatrieme avion, le vol United Airlines 93, s'est ecrase en Pennsylvanie apres que les passagers et l'equipage avaient tente de resister aux terroristes et de reprendre le controle de l'appareil. Ces attentats ont fait 2 977 morts, sans compter les 19 terroristes, et plus de 6 000 blesses. Parmi les victimes figuraient des passagers et des membres d'equipage des avions, des employes du World Trade Center et du Pentagone, ainsi que des centaines de secouristes.

items.title: Ghana must turn horticulture into global export powerhouse – Vice President Naana Jane
items.description: Vice President Prof Jane Naana Opoku Agyemang has challenged Ghana to build a competitive horticulture industry capable of creating jobs, expanding businesses and breaking into global markets. She said Ghana has the capacity to replicate the success of countries such as Kenya if it develops the sector beyond the production of flowers and other horticultural products. “Thank you very much for the references to Kenya. We know we can do same, if not more, can’t we?” she said. Speaking on Saturday at the opening of the 14th Ghana Garden and Flower Show, Prof Naana Jane said horticulture represents a wider economic opportunity involving growers, skills, services, markets and livelihoods. “The opportunity is to help more of these enterprises develop into sustainable businesses that can employ others, supply larger markets, and, where possible, compete beyond Ghana,” she said. She stressed the need for Ghana to move beyond production and strengthen the entire horticultural value chain. “Horticulture is demanding because much of what it produces sometimes is perishable. Therefore, without reliable transport, storage, quality standards, and access to markets, value may be quickly lost,” she said. According to her, government agricultural programmes provide a foundation for expanding the industry. “Under the Feed Ghana Program, vegetables are among priority crops, but with support for irrigation, improved inputs, greenhouse production, and better access to markets, we can do even more,” she said. She added that farmer service centres being established across the country are expected to provide producers with export support, inputs, machinery and market linkages. Prof Naana Jane also linked the expansion of horticulture to Ghana’s environmental agenda, saying the country must make greening an integral part of development. “As part of the Tree for Life initiative launched by His Excellency the President, millions of seedlings are being planted, while our assemblies are being encouraged to work with parks and gardens to improve and maintain green spaces in our towns and cities,” she said. She said young people, in particular, could benefit from opportunities created at the intersection of agriculture, technology, creativity and enterprise. “The opportunity is not only to encourage young people to grow more, but also to help them to see the businesses they can build around their produce,” she said. The Vice President also urged stakeholders to strengthen the standards, financing and market access required for Ghanaian horticultural businesses to compete internationally. “We should build on these foundations,” she said. She further called for greater collaboration among training institutions, financial institutions, the private sector and industry organisations to develop the sector. “Training institutions can develop the skills the sector needs. Financial institutions can support viable enterprises. The private sector can develop markets, and movements such as this one can continue bringing the industry together and making its possibilities visible,” she said. Prof Naana Jane said the recent floods had reinforced the need for Ghana to take environmental protection seriously. “Greening should therefore not be something we consider after development; greening should be part of development itself,” she said. She congratulated Stratcomm Africa, the Ghana Garden and Flower Movement, exhibitors, and others who contributed to organising the 14th Ghana Garden and Flower Show.

items.title: Chelsea face stern Hull test as Blues seek return to winning ways
items.description: Chelsea will look to return to winning ways when they host Hull City at Stamford Bridge today with both sides making strong starts to the Premier League season. Fourth-placed Chelsea against a Hull City side sitting third after three matches. While the Blues have collected six points, Hull have seven and are yet to concede a league goal this season. Chelsea will, however, take confidence from their remarkable record against Hull. The London side have won their last nine meetings in all competitions, while Hull have never won in 18 league visits to Stamford Bridge. The Blues began the season with victories over Fulham and Brighton before suffering a 2-1 defeat away to Arsenal last weekend. They will now be hoping to respond in front of their home supporters. Chelsea have also shown considerable attacking strength, scoring eight goals in their opening three league matches. Their only home league game so far ended in a 4-3 victory over Brighton. João Pedro and Morgan Rogers have been among Chelsea’s notable attacking performers, contributing goals and assists during the opening weeks of the campaign. Chelsea have no reported injury concerns ahead of the match, leaving them with a fully available squad as they attempt to maintain their strong start and close the gap on the teams above them. Hull, meanwhile, have emerged as one of the early surprises of the campaign. They have taken seven points from their opening three matches and, most impressively, have kept three consecutive clean sheets. Their league campaign includes a 2-0 victory over Manchester United and a narrow 1-0 win over Coventry. Although Sunderland eliminated them from the League Cup, their league form remains unbeaten. Goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis has played every minute of Hull’s league campaign and has been instrumental in their perfect defensive record. Hull’s organised defence will face its biggest test yet against a Chelsea attack that has already scored eight times. The visitors will need another disciplined performance if they are to extend their unbeaten league start and end Chelsea’s dominance in this fixture. History, however, strongly favours the hosts. Chelsea have won each of their last nine meetings with Hull and remain unbeaten in 18 league encounters at Stamford Bridge. With Chelsea’s attacking quality and home advantage set against Hull’s impressive defensive record, the match could provide an intriguing contest between the hosts’ firepower and the visitors’ resilience. Chelsea will be expected to start aggressively as they seek to regain momentum after the defeat to Arsenal, with an early lead likely to be central to their approach. items.title: Le président B. D. Faye : « Le Sénégal est un pays qui tient ses promesses et sa jeunesse est sa plus grande richesse »
items.description: La réception de la Flamme olympique au Sénégal prouve, selon le chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, que le Sénégal est un pays qui tient ses promesses et que sa jeunesse est sa plus grande richesse. C’est ce qu’il a soutenu samedi, face aux jeunes athlètes venus accueillir cette flamme au Palais de la République. Le président de la République a accueilli samedi, devant les grilles du Palais, la Flamme olympique devant une assemblée constituée majoritairement de jeunes, notamment des athlètes, dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ) 2026. « Jeunesse du Sénégal, cette flamme que nous venons de recevoir a traversé les mers chez nous. En plus de 100 ans, c'est ma première fois qu’elle arrive sur le sol sénégalais et sur le sol africain. Le monde nous a fait confiance. Il nous a confié ce qu’aucun pays africain n’a reçu, en plus de 100 ans. Voilà pourquoi, de Johannesburg à Nairobi, de Dakar à Djibouti, c’est toute la jeunesse africaine qui vous regarde et qui vous regarde avec confiance et avec fierté », a-t-il dit. Cette confiance qui est placée au Sénégal, souligne le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye, il doit la mériter. « Mais cette flamme que nous avons reçue ce matin dit une chose que j'ai toujours comprise. Elle dit que le Sénégal est un pays qui tient ses promesses et que sa jeunesse est sa plus grande richesse », a-t-il soutenu. Dans quelques semaines, plus de 2700 athlètes fouleront le sol sénégalais. Ils viendront de plus de 206 pays. Dès lors, relève le chef de l’État, ce qu'ils retiendront de la jeunesse sénégalaise, c'est ce qu’elle va montrer. « C'est votre énergie, c'est votre hospitalité, c'est votre terrain. C'est l'image d'un peuple debout qui fait confiance à sa jeunesse et qui la valorise. Rendez-nous fiers et rendez-vous fiers à toute l'Afrique. L'image que les autres retiendront, c'est celle que vous donnerez. Et je veux qu'en partant d'ici, ceux que nous aurons reçus dans cette période retiennent que la jeunesse africaine est débordante d'énergie, qu'elle est debout et déterminée et qu'elle est fière », a-t-il ajouté. Toutefois, le président de la République affirme qu’il fait confiance en sa jeunesse et sait qu’elle relèvera ce défi. Au soir de la journée de clôture de ces jeux, ce qui restera, note-t-il, c'est ce qu’ils auront appris. Les métiers qu’ils maîtriseront mieux, les process qu’ils comprendront davantage. Mais c'est aussi les valeurs de l'olympisme qu’ils auront exaltées. « Mais nous aurons tous la fierté ce soir-là d'avoir démontré que dans la solidarité, nous avons pu relever le défi et nous avons réussi ensemble pour nous et pour l'Afrique. Cette flamme fera bientôt les 14 régions du Sénégal les bras ouverts. Accueillez-la avec espoir, accueillez-la avec fierté, accueillez-la debout et déterminée », a-t-il lancé. Car, relève le président Faye, ce qu’il veut, c’est que ceux qui la portent trouvent dans chaque région du Sénégal une jeunesse debout, une jeunesse fière, une jeunesse prête à relever ce défi. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Mario-a-Lago Kart , Anyone?
items.description: This week, the White House removed a Tetris -inspired game called Build the Wall from its recently launched arcade website after the Tetris Company publicly warned that it takes copyright law “very seriously.” Here are a few options the White House might consider to replace the game: Super PAC-Man Players direct a round creature with a constantly moving mouth through a maze as he munches on tiny coins. Meanwhile, the ghosts of financial lawsuits past pursue Super PAC-Man—but consuming excerpts from favorable Supreme Court rulings allows him to temporarily devour these ghosts, too. Once Super PAC-Man collects all the coins , he progresses, unsatiated, to the next level, where he sends out a single text and all the money starts flowing directly toward him. Words With Enemies Players form new, hateful attacks in this Scrabble-like multiplayer game using letters cut from public-school textbooks, removed museum displays, and maps depicting the former Lake Ontario. Highest-scoring insults include: SCUZZY, ZANY, and LOW-IQ JOKER. Extra points are awarded for letters placed on various Random Capitalization Squares. Mario-a-Lago Kart Up to four players race golf carts around a cartoonishly decorated beach club, crashing through boxes of classified documents to unlock power-ups including nuclear footballs and black markers for unlimited redactions. Between races, players can refuel at the gas pump, assuming they have collected the requisite 175,000 coins per gallon. The winner receives a golf trophy; second, third, and fourth place—as well as any observers or people simply standing nearby—get access to state secrets. Grand Theft Crypto This game is all in the timing: Players must market their own cryptocurrency, then wait until just the right moment to cash out, crashing the currency and tanking other players’ life savings. The Oregon Data Center Modern-day pioneers move into a covered wagon after an eminent-domain order for the construction of a data center displaces them from their hometown. Drinking water is scarce, noise pollution is earsplitting, and morale is low as players try to survive the perilous journey to one of the few remaining corners of protected parkland. Inevitably, all players die when artificial general intelligence bioengineers a new form of dysentery . Goldeneye In this first-person interior-design game, players gild every nook, cranny, and free patch of wall space in their virtual home office. Coal Minecraft No longer beholden to child-labor regulations, players ages 6 to 8 design their own pickaxes before descending 1,500 feet down a shaft to mine bituminous coal. Open-world play means that the only limit is kids’ imagination and black lung and tunnel collapse. Super Smash the Kennedy Center Players battle conservationists, historians, and patrons of the arts atop a revered memorial building, destroying it in the process . Downloadable content expands play to the Reflecting Pool, the National Mall, and the East Wing of the White House. Candy Crush the American Dream Players rearrange foods that were once safe to eat into matching groups to make them disappear as part of an FDA recall . But miss just one, and players will contract a parasitic infection that sends them to the hospital, where they will incur astronomical medical bills, which will prevent them from qualifying for a mortgage, which will force them to move back in with their parents. President Evil A zombie occupies the most powerful office in the world. At the conclusion of Level 2, President Evil might insist that the game isn’t over, but so long as it works as intended, someone else will finally get a turn to play.

items.title: Pro League belge : Tawfik Bentayeb offre la victoire à Anderlecht contre Malines
items.description: Tawfik Bentayeb s’est une nouvelle fois illustré avec Anderlecht. L’attaquant marocain a offert vendredi une précieuse victoire à son équipe sur la pelouse de Malines (0-1), à l’occasion de la 6e journée de la Pro League belge. Dans une rencontre longtemps indécise, les Anderlechtois ont dû faire preuve de patience avant de trouver la faille. C’est finalement le but de Bentayeb, inscrit juste avant la pause, qui a permis aux visiteurs de repartir avec les trois points. Anderlecht a connu un début de match compliqué, avec plusieurs fautes commises dans les premières minutes. Giulian Biancone a notamment été averti dès la 5e minute, tandis que Malines tentait de profiter des difficultés de son adversaire pour mettre la pression sur la défense bruxelloise. Les locaux ont notamment cherché à jouer rapidement vers l’avant en utilisant des ballons aériens, obligeant la défense d’Anderlecht à rester vigilante. Alors que les deux équipes semblaient se diriger vers une pause sur un score nul, Tawfik Bentayeb a finalement fait la différence. À la 43e minute, l’attaquant marocain s’est parfaitement positionné dans le petit rectangle pour reprendre un centre à ras de terre d’Ilias Koutsoupias et envoyer le ballon au fond des filets. | Tawfik Bentayeb rondt een knappe collectieve aanval af. #KVMAND Bekijk alle #JPL -doelpunten in de DAZN-app! pic.twitter.com/iEamf34eIw — DAZN België (@DAZN_BENL) September 11, 2026 Une réalisation qui récompense une belle séquence collective des Mauves et permet à Anderlecht de prendre l’avantage au meilleur moment. Au retour des vestiaires, Malines a d’abord adopté une approche prudente avant de progressivement prendre davantage de risques. Confrontés à l’obligation de revenir au score, les joueurs locaux ont tenté d’accentuer la pression sur la défense anderlechtoise. Anderlecht a néanmoins su conserver son avantage et gérer les assauts adverses. Malgré les tentatives de Malines pour égaliser, les visiteurs ont résisté jusqu’au coup de sifflet final. Grâce à ce succès, Anderlecht décroche ainsi sa première victoire à l’extérieur de la saison et réalise une bonne opération au classement. Anderlecht remonte au classement Avec ces trois points supplémentaires, Anderlecht totalise désormais 10 points après six journées et occupe la 7e place de la Pro League belge. Malines connaît en revanche un début de saison beaucoup plus compliqué. Le club reste 15e avec seulement deux points au compteur, une situation qui accentue la pression avant les prochaines journées. Pour Bentayeb, cette nouvelle prestation vient confirmer son importance dans le secteur offensif d’Anderlecht. En inscrivant l’unique but de la rencontre dans un déplacement difficile, l’international marocain a une nouvelle fois démontré sa capacité à se montrer décisif dans les moments importants. Son but pourrait également constituer un nouveau tournant dans sa saison, alors qu’Anderlecht cherchera désormais à enchaîner les résultats positifs afin de se rapprocher des premières places du championnat. The post Pro League belge : Tawfik Bentayeb offre la victoire à Anderlecht contre Malines appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Pour contrer Huawei en Afrique, Washington accorde un prêt de 100 millions de dollars à Africell
items.description: L'administration americaine va accorder un pret de pres de 100 millions de dollars a Africell, dans le cadre des efforts de Washington pour freiner l'expansion du groupe chinois Huawei dans les infrastructures telecoms africaines, selon un communique et une source proche du dossier cites le 11 septembre par Reuters. Le financement sera accorde par l'Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM), l'organisme americain de credit a l'exportation. Il doit permettre a Africell d'investir dans les dernieres technologies de reseaux mobiles proposees par des fournisseurs americains et leurs partenaires. « Nous sommes heureux de travailler avec l'EXIM pour introduire des infrastructures de communication plus fiables et securisees sur nos marches », a declare Ziad Dalloul, directeur general d'Africell Holding Limited. Washington veut reduire la presence de Huawei Ce pret s'inscrit dans la strategie americaine visant a favoriser l'utilisation de technologies telecoms autres que celles de Huawei a l'etranger. Washington accuse depuis plusieurs annees le groupe chinois de presenter des risques pour la securite et l'espionnage, des accusations rejetees par Huawei. Selon Counterpoint Research, Huawei detenait environ 52 % du marche des infrastructures 5G en Afrique. L'administration Trump avait lance des son premier mandat une initiative visant a limiter la presence des technologies, applications et equipements telecoms chinois dans les infrastructures americaines et celles de ses allies. Cette politique s'est poursuivie lors du second mandat de Donald Trump. Le nouveau pret s'inscrit egalement dans le prolongement d'un decret signe en 2025 par le president americain, demandant aux agences federales de promouvoir a l'etranger les technologies americaines dans plusieurs secteurs, notamment l'intelligence artificielle, les centres de donnees, le cloud et les reseaux. Africell, un operateur present dans quatre pays africains Fonde en 2001, Africell est present en Angola, en Gambie, en Republique democratique du Congo et en Sierra Leone, ou il revendique environ 15 millions de clients. L'entreprise a notamment fait appel a des groupes comme HP, Nokia, Dell et Oracle pour equiper un nouveau centre de donnees en Angola. Le groupe avait deja beneficie, en 2018, d'un pret de 100 millions de dollars accorde par l'Overseas Private Investment Corporation, ancien organisme americain de financement du developpement aujourd'hui integre a la Development Finance Corporation. La Chine defend, pour sa part, ses investissements en Afrique. L'ambassade chinoise a Washington a affirme que ceux-ci avaient contribue a la croissance du continent et etaient bien accueillis par les populations. Elle a appele les etats-Unis a soutenir davantage le developpement des pays africains plutot qu'a mener une politique visant a « saper la cooperation sino-africaine ».

items.title: École nationale des Sous-officiers de Gendarmerie : 300 nouveaux sous-officiers reçoivent leurs épaulettes de fin de formation
items.description: L’Ecole Nationale des Sous-Officiers de la Gendarmerie a vibré, ce 11 septembre 2026, au rythme d’une cérémonie solennelle marquant la fin de formation de la promotion « KAWGU ». À cette occasion, 300 nouveaux sous-officiers, dont 15 personnels féminins, ont reçu leurs épaulettes, symbole de l’aboutissement d’un parcours de formation exigeant et du début de leur carrière au service de la Nation. Placée sous la présidence du Camarade Général de Division Célestin SIMPORÉ, Ministre d’État, Ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense Patriotique, la cérémonie a connu la participation d’importantes personnalités. Parmi elles figuraient plusieurs membres du Gouvernement, des autorités administratives et judiciaires, ainsi que des autorités coutumières et religieuses. Parents, amis et connaissances, venus de divers horizons, ont également répondu présents pour partager avec les nouveaux Maréchaux des Logis ce moment particulièrement solennel. Le Camarade Chef de Bataillon Ismaël SOMBIE, Ministre d’État, Ministre de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources Animales et Halieutiques, parrain de la promotion, a apporté son accompagnement et ses encouragements aux nouveaux sous-officiers. La cérémonie a été ponctuée par plusieurs temps forts. Prenant la parole au nom de sa promotion, l’Élève Sous-Officier ZONGO Jean Donald est revenu sur le chemin parcouru avec ses camarades depuis l’entrée à l’École, le 26 octobre 2024. Il a ensuite invité ses camarades à rester convaincus, convaincants et déterminés face aux réalités du terrain qui les attend. Le Commandant de l’École Nationale des Sous-Officiers de la Gendarmerie, le Chef d’Escadron COULIBALY Souleymane, a quant à lui dressé le bilan de deux années de formation articulées autour de trois dimensions indissociables : la formation morale, la formation physique et la formation intellectuelle et professionnelle, complétées par des stages pratiques et des mises en condition opérationnelle. Il a annoncé un taux de réussite de 100 % à l’examen final, avec une moyenne de classe de 15,436 sur 20. S’adressant directement aux jeunes sous-officiers, il leur a rappelé qu’un diplôme sanctionne une formation mais ne consacre jamais définitivement une compétence, les invitant donc à entretenir sans cesse les connaissances reçues à l’épreuve du terrain. Dans son allocution, le Camarade Colonel Issa YAGUIBOU, Chef d’État-Major de la Gendarmerie Nationale, a, au nom de l’ensemble du personnel de l’institution, renouvelé l’engagement de la Gendarmerie à poursuivre avec patriotisme, loyauté et discipline l’exécution des missions qui lui sont assignées. Il a salué le leadership du Chef de l’État, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, et remercié le Ministre d’État, Ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense Patriotique, ainsi que le parrain de la promotion, pour leur sens de l’écoute et leur sacrifice envers la Nation. S’adressant aux nouveaux Maréchaux des Logis, il a rappelé que l’épaulette n’est pas un privilège mais une responsabilité accrue envers le peuple, appelant à une rupture totale avec la corruption, le favoritisme et l’abus d’autorité. Il a annoncé que chaque sous-officier de la promotion recevra le manifeste de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire, appelé à devenir leur bréviaire. Il a enfin adressé ses félicitations au commandement de l’École et exprimé sa reconnaissance aux familles pour leurs sacrifices. Les invités ont pu apprécier une démonstration de savoirs et de savoir-faire réalisée par les élèves en fin de formation, à travers un numéro de carrousel. Cette prestation a mis en évidence les compétences que ces jeunes Maréchaux des Logis ont acquises au cours de leur passage à l’École Nationale des Sous-Officiers de la Gendarmerie. Le cérémonial s’est poursuivi avec le traditionnel défilé militaire, exécuté avec rigueur et discipline par ces nouveaux Maréchaux des Logis de l’École Nationale des Sous-Officiers de la Gendarmerie, en compagnie d’autres écoles et centres de formation des Forces armées nationales, à savoir les écoles sœurs que sont le Groupement d’Instruction des Forces Armées (GIFA), l’École Nationale des Sapeurs-Pompiers (ENASAP) et le Centre d’Instruction et de Formation Militaire de l’Armée de l’Air (CIFMAA). Cette séquence, tout aussi symbolique, a traduit la cohésion, la détermination et la disponibilité de la nouvelle promotion à répondre, aux côtés des autres forces, aux différentes missions. En choisissant le nom de baptême « KAWGU », victoire en langue fulfuldé, ce nom prend tout son sens au moment où notre chère Patrie lutte efficacement contre l’hydre terroriste qui tenaille le vivre-ensemble et la quiétude des populations. Ces jeunes Maréchaux des Logis nouvellement promus aligneront sans doute l’acte à la parole donnée, en contribuant significativement à la restauration totale de la Patrie et à la lutte contre l’insécurité sous toutes ses formes. En marge de cette sortie officielle, la 52ème promotion des Élèves Sous-Officiers de Gendarmerie a prêté serment devant le Tribunal de Grande Instance de Bobo-Dioulasso, le 10 septembre 2026. La gendarmerie nationale, une force humaine !

items.title: PML-N's Rana Sanaullah says Parliament to decide on more provinces
items.description: Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Saturday that Parliament will decide on the matter of creating new provinces. The recent debate regarding new provinces began in late July when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called for new provinces as part of reforms to the current governance system, drawing strong reactions from government ministers. During a press conference in Lahore, Sanaullah was asked about Naqvi’s recent remarks where he said that “new administrative units will eventually have to be created as Pakistan’s growing population and changing needs can no longer be effectively managed through the existing administrative structure”. The PML-N leader replied that making such statements at business seminars or conferences had not resulted in any “improvement” in the situation. “In my humble opinion, this debate should have been started in Parliament,” he said, adding that issues of such magnitude should not be reduced to speeches, social media, seminars or business forums. “The outcome will also emerge in Parliament,” the PM’s adviser said, adding that the “matter will be resolved in a better direction” when all political parties and the leadership of all provinces discuss it. “In any circumstance, the decision of whether any province will be created or not will be made in Parliament, and by Parliament,” Sanaullah reiterated. He also stressed that Naqvi, in his remarks, had said the creation of new provinces depended on whether the public wanted it . “If the public wants, then no one can stop it. The decision of whether the public wants it or not can only be made in Parliament,” the PML-N leader said. Sanaullah said his party was deliberating upon the matter and will issue a policy statement after participating in the debate and once it “comes to a proper place where a result could emerge”. The PM’s aide further said that no minister had raised the matter before the federal cabinet so far, adding that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif would issue the appropriate directives once the topic is discussed. He emphasised that even if a referendum were to be held to gauge public opinion, it would require approval by the parliament. He remarked that the PML-N was not “bound” to issue a statement on the topic of new provinces merely based on economic forums. Referring to the Sindh Assembly’s adoption of a resolution against dividing the province, Sanaullah said the PPP had “overreacted”. Coalition partners to resolve differences Speaking on the recent rift between the PPP and the PML-N, the minister said differences between the two parties had, by and large, been resolved. Sanaullah, who is also a member of the core committees formed to resolve differences between the two major coalition partners, said after attending a meeting at Governor House that any remaining issues would be settled amicably, as both sides were committed to resolving them. “Ideally, the core committees should meet every month, but this could not happen due to the elections in GB and AJK. Meetings will now hopefully be held more regularly to smooth over any old or new rough patches,” he said. He attributed the tensions mainly to emotionally charged election campaigns in Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir , saying the campaigns were now over and so were the frictions. The PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre, has strongly opposed the suggested move to carve out Karachi as a separate province. PML-N’s Khawaja Asif, who had earlier noted that the appropriate forum for such a discussion was the parliament, said last week that devolution of power was “ inevitable ”. The opposition parties, including the PTI, have said they will hold consultations to call an all-parties conference to discuss several issues, including the creation of new provinces, law and order and the economy. PTI, JI marches to Islamabad Asked about the plans of the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) and the PTI to march towards Islamabad on September 20 and 27, respectively, Sanaullah remarked that the JI’s past political activities had been peaceful while the same could not be expected from the PTI. “Everyone knows that JI is a political party and it has always carried out its activities according to the Constitutional and legal requirements,” he said. He affirmed that the government “respected” political protests and therefore had held negotiations with the JI during which its representatives “carefully and seriously listened to their demands”. The PM’s adviser urged JI leaders not to “overwork themselves needlessly” as the PML-N and PM Shehbaz also wanted a reduction in the fuel prices and electricity bills “as much as and even more than JI did”. On the other hand, Sanaullah said the government had “no expectation” that the PTI’s long march would remain peaceful and referred to remarks made by its leaders. “If they are coming to Islamabad to overthrow the government and if this is their intention and thinking, then it is obvious that they will carry out violence after coming there,” he asserted. “Based on these reports, our assessment is that it could be a replay of May 9. If it takes that route and assumes a similar proportion, it would be very unfortunate. Since the matter is also before the courts, the government is awaiting their decisions before finalising its strategy. But one thing is certain: violence cannot be allowed,” he said. Additional input from Ahmed Faraz

items.title: The Joy of Being Asked to Help
items.description: This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. Learning how to drive is a rare instance in a teenager’s life, Liz Krieger argues in a recent article: “This wobbly uncertainty, this return to a kind of innocence, is the rarest condition in a 16-year-old, and it lasts about as long as a learner’s permit does.” The best part of teaching her daughter how to drive, Krieger writes, is being allowed to help. Even once we move beyond the fierce teenage desire for independence, asking for assistance can feel awkward and vulnerable—espsecially in America’s culture of individualism, Julie Beck noted last year. But deciding to go it alone ends up depriving loved ones of the joy of participating. “Pushing through discomfort to accept the help that was offered” in planning her wedding, Julie wrote, made it “feel less like a product we had purchased and more like something special that we had created with our friends, family, and neighbors.” Today’s newsletter explores what asking for help does for the people helping. On Asking for Help The Last Thing Teenagers Will Let You Teach Them By Liz Krieger An interesting shift happens when a kid is learning to drive, and you’re both inside a box with your fear, moving 40 miles an hour. Read the article. To Make Someone Happy, Ask for Help By Arthur C. Brooks Generosity is like the circulation of the blood, healthiest and best when it goes around and around. Read the article. A Wedding Reveals How Much Help Is Really Available to You By Julie Beck Big life moments offer permission to ask for assistance. You should seize it. Read the article. Still Curious? Coaching is the new “asking your friends for help” : Lifestyle coaches offer help with vacation planning, decision making, meditation, and more—for a price, Olga Khazan wrote last year. The one big thing you can do for your kids : Research shows that you probably have less effect on your kids than you think—with one major exception, Arthur C. Brooks wrote in 2024. Other Diversions Seven books that will make you put down your phone ( From 2023 ) What makes tennis one of the greatest games Okay, sure, a folding iPhone PS I recently asked readers to share a photo of something that sparks their sense of awe in the world. “It was a beautiful clear day when my husband and I were driving south from Seattle on Interstate 5 (he was driving),” Pat B., from Bellingham, Washington, wrote. “I saw Mount Rainier appearing to float serenely above the traffic below. The contrast between the immutable and the transitory was awesome!” I’ll continue to feature your responses in the coming weeks. — Isabel

items.title: Corée du Sud-Afrique : la Banque africaine de développement mise sur les minéraux critiques et l’intelligence artificielle
items.description: La Banque africaine de developpement (BAD) a presente cinq projets regionaux de developpement des mineraux critiques a des entreprises et institutions financieres sud-coreennes, lors d'un dialogue de haut niveau organise le 8 septembre a Seoul, en marge de la 8e Conference ministerielle de la Cooperation economique Coree-Afrique (KOAFEC). Conduite par le president du Groupe de la BAD, Sidi Ould Tah, la rencontre visait a rapprocher le secteur prive coreen des opportunites d'investissement en Afrique, notamment dans les infrastructures, l'energie, les technologies numeriques, l'industrie manufacturiere et les chaînes de valeur liees aux ressources minieres. La BAD a insiste sur l'importance des mineraux critiques pour la transition energetique mondiale et la production de technologies propres. Son president a appele a depasser l'exportation brute des matieres premieres afin de developper davantage leur transformation et leur raffinage sur le continent, avec l'objectif d'y creer davantage d'emplois et de valeur ajoutee. Les cinq projets presentes couvrent plusieurs regions d'Afrique. La Banque africaine de developpement a egalement detaille ses mecanismes de garantie, de cofinancement et d'attenuation des risques destines a faciliter l'investissement prive et a rendre les projets africains plus attractifs pour les investisseurs. Un partenariat renforce dans le numerique et l'IA La cooperation entre la Coree du Sud et l'Afrique s'est egalement renforcee dans le domaine du numerique a l'occasion de la cloture de la conference, le 11 septembre. La BAD et Seoul ont signe deux nouveaux accords, dont un memorandum d'entente portant sur la cooperation dans le financement et la preparation de projets et programmes gouvernementaux. Une lettre d'intention concerne par ailleurs la cooperation dans l'intelligence artificielle et le numerique. Les deux parties prevoient notamment la creation d'un hub africain consacre a l'intelligence artificielle. Cette plateforme doit permettre de federer differentes initiatives, de centraliser les ressources et les projets et de contribuer a la formation de nouveaux talents ainsi qu'au developpement des infrastructures numeriques. En contrepartie, la Coree du Sud cherche a securiser son acces aux ressources minieres africaines necessaires a ses industries de haute technologie, notamment dans le secteur des semi-conducteurs.

Visite d’État en Côte d’Ivoire : Mamadi Doumbouya accueilli dans une ambiance fraternelle à Abidjan
items.description: Le Président de la République de Guinée, le Général Mamadi Doumbouya, est arrivé à Abidjan vendredi 11 septembre 2026, pour une visite d’État placée sous le signe du renforcement des liens d’amitié et de coopération entre la Guinée et la Côte d’Ivoire. À l’aéroport international Félix-Houphouët-Boigny, le Chef de l’État guinéen a été accueilli par la Présidente du Sénat ivoirien, Kandia Camara, accompagnée de plusieurs membres du Gouvernement. L’Ambassadeur de Guinée en Côte d’Ivoire, Bachir Diallo, était également présent aux côtés des autorités ivoiriennes. Au pavillon présidentiel, Mamadi Doumbouya a eu de chaleureux échanges avec les représentants du Président Alassane Ouattara, dans une atmosphère empreinte de cordialité. Mais c’est surtout la mobilisation de la communauté guinéenne qui a marqué les esprits. Nombreux, des Guinéens vivant en Côte d’Ivoire — hommes, femmes, jeunes et familles — ont fait le déplacement pour réserver un accueil chaleureux au Président de la République. Allant à leur rencontre, Mamadi Doumbouya a salué plusieurs compatriotes et partagé avec eux quelques instants de communion. Cette forte mobilisation témoigne de l’attachement de la diaspora à la Guinée, mais aussi de la profondeur des liens humains entre les peuples guinéen et ivoirien. Cette visite d’État s’annonce ainsi comme une nouvelle étape dans le raffermissement de l’axe Conakry-Abidjan, fondé sur l’histoire, la fraternité et des intérêts communs.

items.title: List of countries offering eVisa to Nigerians in 2026
items.description: Nigerian passport holders can travel to a number of countries by applying for a visa electronically instead of visiting an embassy or submitting a traditional paper visa application. An eVisa is generally an electronic travel document that is applied for online before travelling. However, requirements, processing times, fees and permitted length of stay vary from one country to another. According to current passport and visa data, Nigerians have access to dozens of destinations offering eVisa or online visa facilities. Passport Index currently lists countries including Djibouti, Ecuador and El Salvador among destinations offering eVisa access to Nigerian passport holders. Below are some destinations Nigerians can consider when looking for an online visa route. 1. South Africa South Africa operates an online eVisa system through its Department of Home Affairs. Applicants can create a profile, complete the application online, upload supporting documents and make payment electronically. The South African government says the eVisa is an electronic document linked to the traveller’s passport and serves as an alternative to obtaining a traditional visa through an embassy or consulate. Applicants using the online system must meet the country’s eligibility requirements and use designated airports for the eVisa programme. 2. Rwanda Rwanda allows travellers to apply for visas online through its immigration system. The country’s Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration says foreigners can apply for a visitor visa online, at an immigration office or through a Rwandan diplomatic mission. Rwanda also allows nationals of all countries to obtain visas on arrival, while certain nationalities—including Nigerians—benefit from visa-fee waivers under the country’s arrangements for African Union, Commonwealth and La Francophonie members. For Nigerians specifically, Rwanda has confirmed that the country has long provided a 30-day visa-free arrangement to Nigerian citizens. Therefore, Nigerians travelling to Rwanda generally do not need to apply for an eVisa for a short visit. 3. Djibouti Djibouti is another destination listed as offering eVisa access to Nigerian passport holders. Passport Index currently lists Djibouti as offering both an eVisa and visa-on-arrival option for Nigerians. Travellers should check the Djiboutian authorities’ current requirements before applying, including passport validity, supporting documents and permitted duration of stay. 4. Ecuador Ecuador is listed among countries offering an electronic visa route to Nigerian passport holders. Current passport information lists Ecuador as an eVisa destination for Nigerians. However, an online visa application does not mean automatic approval. Applicants must satisfy the country’s immigration requirements before travelling. 5. El Salvador Nigerian passport holders can also use an electronic visa route for El Salvador, according to current passport information. Passport Index lists El Salvador as an eVisa destination for Nigerians. Travellers should confirm the current application requirements and whether additional documents or approvals are required before booking a flight. 6. Equatorial Guinea Equatorial Guinea is another African destination listed as offering an eVisa facility to Nigerian citizens. The electronic application route can reduce the need for applicants to begin the process through a traditional embassy application. Applicants should nevertheless confirm the current entry conditions before travelling because visa rules can change. 7. Cambodia Cambodia is among the Asian destinations where Nigerian passport holders can access an electronic visa route. Current 2026 passport information lists Cambodia as an eVisa destination for Nigerians, with a stay of up to 30 days indicated for the eVisa category. The eVisa should be obtained before travelling and presented according to Cambodia’s entry requirements. 8. Malaysia Malaysia is also listed among destinations providing an electronic visa facility to Nigerian passport holders. Current visa data lists Malaysia under the eVisa category for Nigerians, with a 14-day stay indicated. Travellers should check the latest Malaysian immigration requirements before submitting an application. 9. Qatar Nigerian passport holders are also listed as eligible for an online visa route to Qatar. Current passport data places Qatar among destinations offering eVisa access to Nigerians. Applicants should confirm the appropriate visa category and supporting requirements before making travel arrangements. 10. United Arab Emirates The United Arab Emirates offers electronic visa application routes for eligible foreign travellers, although the exact process depends on the applicant’s circumstances and visa category. Nigerian travellers should pay particular attention to the applicable eligibility conditions because UAE entry-visa rules differ according to nationality, visa type and other circumstances. The UAE’s Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security continues to update its entry-visa eligibility framework. 11. Australia Australia operates an electronic visa system, although Nigerians should not assume that an online application means an automatic or simplified approval. Current Nigerian passport visa data lists Australia among destinations with an electronic visa/online authorisation route. Applicants must meet Australia’s immigration requirements and provide the documents requested during the application process. 12. Albania Albania is another European destination listed as offering an eVisa route to Nigerian passport holders. This can be particularly useful for Nigerians looking for destinations where the visa application process can be initiated electronically rather than through a traditional paper application. 13. Serbia Serbia is also listed among European destinations offering an eVisa route for Nigerian citizens. Applicants should verify the latest Serbian entry rules before making travel arrangements. 14. Moldova Moldova is another European destination included in current eVisa listings for Nigerian passport holders. The electronic application process means eligible applicants can begin the visa process online. 15. Bahrain Bahrain is among the Middle Eastern destinations listed as offering an eVisa facility to Nigerian passport holders. Travellers should check the official Bahraini immigration portal for the applicable visa category, fees and documentation. Other countries offering online visa routes Current 2026 passport data also lists several other destinations where Nigerians can access eVisa or electronic visa facilities, including: Angola Botswana Burundi Democratic Republic of Congo Ethiopia Gabon Madagascar Malawi Mauritania Namibia São Tomé and Príncipe Somalia South Sudan Tanzania Uganda Zambia Zimbabwe Bhutan Indonesia Kazakhstan Kyrgyzstan Oman Pakistan Singapore South Korea Thailand Vietnam Antigua and Barbuda Bahamas Nicaragua Trinidad and Tobago Bolivia Chile Colombia Guyana Suriname Venezuela The precise classification varies by source because some countries use an eVisa, while others use an electronic travel authorisation or an online application followed by another stage of processing. Current visa databases therefore produce slightly different totals. One current database, for example, lists 56 eVisa destinations for Nigerian passport holders, while another lists 60. What Nigerians should know before applying An eVisa does not mean visa-free entry. Instead, it means the traveller can apply electronically before the journey, rather than necessarily visiting an embassy to submit a traditional visa application. The post List of countries offering eVisa to Nigerians in 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Atiku’s subsidy plan failed under Obasanjo – Presidency
items.description: The Presidency has said that Atiku Abubakar’s plan to subsidise crude for local refineries failed when it implemented under former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration. Read Also: Atiku backs Dangote, says subsidy proposal only for local refineries Otega Ogra, Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on digital and new media, made the point while reacting to the proposal by the former vice-president for a production subsidy for local refineries. Ogra wrote on X (Twitter): “Excuse me, sir. Nigeria already tried your production-subsidy to local refineries idea while you were Vice President. We know the shambolic results of that production subsidy. You know it too.” Ogra said Warri refinery’s utilisation fell to 14.27 percent in 2003 and 9.1 percent in 2004, while Kaduna refinery recorded 15.96 percent and 26 percent, respectively. He said Port Harcourt refinery’s utilisation also dropped from 60.73 percent in 2001 to 31.04 percent in 2004. “Meanwhile, price of petrol more than tripled by 2004 and nearly quadrupled by the time you left office despite your production subsidy to local refiners. “On October 9, 2003, your same administration cancelled the discount itself through Presidential directive PRES/158. “President Obasanjo ordered NNPC to pay full international price for refinery crude. Your production subsidy was tried, failed and scrapped, with you as Vice President. “So, before selling Nigerians this failed production subsidy policy again, answer one simple question. “I know there are many Nigerians who were too young to know what was happening then. But if you may tell them, where is the evidence that it worked the first time? “It’s still the same theory you practiced then, and we haven’t changed country yet. “One thing we already have, are the failed results of that experiment, Alhaji.” Vanguard News The post Atiku’s subsidy plan failed under Obasanjo – Presidency appeared first on Vanguard News .
